events.arc: The River Ice in the Ninth Month
events.text: At the river crossing an old ferryman is pulling his boat up for the winter. 'Ice soon,' he says. 'Grey ice holds a cat, white holds a dog, black holds nothing. Remember it, traveller. The river takes someone every winter.'

choices.text: Thank him and remember it

effects.log: You say it over to yourself on the road: grey, white, black. The ferryman nods as if you had passed a test.

choices.text: Ask who it took last winter

effects.log: 'A salt merchant with a heavy cart, in a hurry.' The ferryman spits into the water. 'Hurry is what the river eats.'

choices.text: Help him haul the boat up the bank

effects.log: It takes both of you and a mule. He gives you a cup of hot water with ginger in it and says your back is good for something.

events.arc: The River Ice in the Ninth Month
events.text: Winter. You must cross the frozen river before dark or sleep in the snow. The ice ahead is grey near the bank, white in the middle, and in one long seam where the current runs underneath it is black and shining.

choices.text: Cross on the grey and white, around the black seam

effects.log: It takes an hour, zigzagging, testing each step. The ice groans under you twice. You reach the far bank at dusk, knees shaking, alive.

choices.text: Run straight across the black seam to save time

ok.log: The black ice bends like cloth under your feet and holds, just. You are across before the crack catches you. You sit on the bank and cannot stop laughing.

fail.deathCause: the black ice of the winter river
fail.log: The black ice opens like a mouth. The cold is a hammer. You claw out onto the white ice with numb hands and lie there, barely breathing.

choices.text: Read the ice the way the ferryman taught a child once

effects.log: Grey holds a cat. White holds a dog. You hear the old voice and walk the safe ice like a road, without a single groan from the river.

choices.text: Sleep in the snow and cross at dawn, when it is coldest

effects.log: A bitter night in a hollow under the bank. At dawn the ice is grey all over, and you cross it like a floor.

events.arc: The River Ice in the Ninth Month
events.text: On the frozen river a cart has gone through the black seam. A mule is thrashing in the hole, a carter is clinging to the edge, and the crack is spreading toward the carter's child, who is standing on the white ice, frozen with fear.

choices.text: Lie flat, slide out, and pull the child back first

effects.log: You spread your weight on the ice like the ferryman said, reach the child, and slide back together. The carter climbs out on the cart shafts. The mule is lost.

choices.text: Run out and haul the carter out of the water

ok.log: You heave the carter out by the collar onto good ice, grab the child, and drag them both to the bank. The carter weeps and calls on every god.

fail.deathCause: the black ice of the winter river
fail.log: The edge breaks under your knees and you go in to the chest. The carter gets out over your back. You barely get out yourself.

choices.text: Throw your belt and a rope from the bank

effects.log: Rope, belt, and the cart's own reins knotted together. You pull the carter out, then the child, slowly, from the safety of the grey ice.

events.arc: The River Ice in the Ninth Month
events.text: The carter you met on the ice, years ago, has found you at an inn, with a sack of the year's first rice and a much bigger child, who stands very straight and bows. 'This one,' says the carter, 'wanted to say it in person.'

choices.text: Accept the rice and the bow

effects.log: The child says thank you, then asks how you knew to lie flat on the ice. You tell about the ferryman, and the three colours. The child repeats it, three times.

choices.text: Refuse the rice and buy them dinner instead

effects.log: The carter protests the whole meal and eats very well. The child eats even better.

choices.text: Ask about the river this winter

effects.log: 'Thin,' says the carter. 'They put a rope across the crossing now. Every winter. They call it the traveller's rope.' You did not know that. You are glad.

events.text: The villages under Broken Pass have shut their doors at sunset for a month. A tiger has taken goats, then a dog from a doorstep, then a woodcutter's coat, which was found on the path, empty and torn. The hunters say this tiger has learned that people are easy.

choices.text: Listen to the hunters' stories

effects.log: Pugmarks as wide as a plate. A limp in the left hind foot from an old trap. It hunts at dusk, upwind. You will remember all of it.

choices.text: Offer to help the villages

effects.log: The headman looks at you with hope that is hard to bear. 'Then be careful. The last brave one is still missing.'

choices.text: Take the long road round the pass

effects.log: Three days longer, and safe. In the inn at the end of it you hear that the tiger took a pedlar on the pass road that same week.

events.text: Dusk on the pass road. The birds have gone quiet. In the mud ahead, a pugmark as wide as a plate, the left hind print dragging. It is fresh. The wind is at your back, carrying your scent forward to wherever it is waiting.

choices.text: Turn back and walk downhill, slowly, never running

effects.log: Running is what prey does. You walk. Something big moves in the bamboo beside the road, keeping pace, and then, at the first lit house, stops. You do not sleep that night.

choices.text: Climb the old pine and wait it out

ok.log: You are up the pine before you know you have moved. The tiger comes out of the bamboo, huge, and circles the tree until dawn, and goes. You climb down at noon.

fail.deathCause: the tiger of Broken Pass
fail.log: A branch snaps. You fall into the brush and the tiger's paw opens your shoulder before you scramble back up the trunk. You cling there all night, bleeding.

choices.text: Turn to face the wind and go upwind of it

effects.log: You remember: it hunts upwind. You cut across the slope so your scent goes away from the bamboo. It loses you. You hear it cough, angry, far below.

events.text: The villagers have built a pit trap on the tiger's path, and need someone to sit by it at dusk as bait in a cage of bamboo, to lure it. The cage is flimsy. The headman will not ask. He only looks at you.

choices.text: Sit in the cage

ok.log: It comes at full dark. The cage shakes like a drum. Then the ground gives under it, and the tiger is in the pit, roaring. The villages light fires on every hill.

fail.deathCause: the tiger of Broken Pass
fail.log: It misses the pit and comes straight at the cage. The bamboo breaks. You fight your way out with a torch and a lot of luck, and it flees, burned.

choices.text: Tie a goat in the cage instead, and wait nearby with a torch

effects.log: The goat yells all night. The tiger comes, circles, smells you, and goes. At least the goat lives. The tiger is still out there.

choices.text: Hunt it in its own den with the best hunters

ok.log: You track it to a cave above the waterfall and drive it out into the hunters' spears. The pass is open again.

fail.deathCause: the tiger of Broken Pass
fail.log: The den is too dark and the tiger too quick. Two hunters are hurt carrying you out.

choices.text: Persuade the villages to clear the bamboo around the houses

effects.log: No cover, no ambush. It takes all month. The tiger loses its advantage, gets hungry, and moves on to another valley. Not a victory. Lives saved.

events.text: In the cave above the waterfall, where the tiger of Broken Pass lived, there is a sound. A cub, alone, hungry, hissing at you with all its tiny fury.

choices.text: Carry it to the temple monks to raise

effects.log: The monks are horrified, then charmed. It grows up behind the temple wall, fat on rice and fish, and never learns that people are easy.

choices.text: Leave it meat and let the mountain raise it

effects.log: You leave a hare at the cave mouth every few days until it can hunt. It is wild. It stays away from the villages. You hope.

choices.text: Take it to the county to sell as a curiosity

effects.log: A rich man buys it for his garden. It is well fed and very bored. You do not visit.

events.arc: The Cracks in the Willow Dam
events.text: Above Willow Village the old earth dam holds back a lake of spring snowmelt. Walking its top, you notice water seeping through the downstream face in three places, clear and fast, as if the dam is weeping.

choices.text: Tell the village headman

effects.log: The headman listens politely and says the dam has stood for a hundred years. It is planting season. Nobody has time.

choices.text: Mark the seeps with sticks and measure them for a week

effects.log: By the end of the week the seeps are twice as fast and one of them is cloudy now, carrying earth. That is the bad sign. You know it is.

choices.text: Not your village, not your dam

effects.log: You go on your way. A month later you hear the name Willow Village spoken in a teahouse in a low voice.

events.arc: The Cracks in the Willow Dam
events.text: Night rain for six days. You have come back to Willow Village. The seeps in the dam face are roaring now, brown with earth, and the top of the dam is sagging in the middle like an old horse's back.

choices.text: Run through the village banging on doors

effects.log: Door after door, shouting. Some curse you. Most come. The ones who saw your sticks last spring come first, with their children on their backs.

choices.text: Shore up the dam face with sandbags and timber

ok.log: You and a dozen farmers pile sacks and timber against the worst of it all night. It holds until dawn, until everyone is out, and then it goes.

fail.deathCause: the Willow Dam breaking
fail.log: The face slumps under you and you are carried down in a wave of mud. You fetch up against a tree half a li away, half drowned.

choices.text: Show the headman the cloudy seep you marked

effects.log: The headman looks at your marks, at the brown water, and goes grey. He rings the temple bell himself. The whole village is on the hill within the hour.

events.arc: The Cracks in the Willow Dam
events.text: The Willow Dam is gone and the village is rebuilding on the hill. The headman, older, finds you, and asks whether you will help them build the new dam properly this time.

choices.text: Help them build it with stone at the core

effects.log: Stone core, clay face, a spillway for the floods. It takes three years of summers. When it is finished, they carve your name on the spillway stone.

choices.text: Teach them to watch the seeps

effects.log: Every spring, a child walks the dam with sticks. The job is called the dam's ear. It is a great honour in Willow Village.

choices.text: Move on; they will manage

effects.log: They do. The new dam is a little crooked and holds anyway. The headman sends you a jar of the village's pickled radish every New Year.

events.text: A lonely inn on the northern road. The innkeeper is nailing the shutters closed at noon. 'Wolf winter,' he says. 'They came down last night and killed the dog on its chain. They will be back. They are thin, and they are many.'

choices.text: Help nail the shutters

effects.log: You work until dark. The innkeeper gives you the room over the stable, the warmest. Outside the snow starts, and keeps on starting.

choices.text: Ask how many

effects.log: 'Twenty. More. The old ones say a white wolf leads them, and the white one is clever.' He hammers another nail. 'Do not go to the privy at night.'

choices.text: Push on before the snow

effects.log: You make the next town just before the snow closes the road. The inn, you hear later, was under siege for nine days.

events.text: Snowed in for six days. The firewood is gone. Out in the drifts, the wolves sit in a ring around the inn, patient. The woodpile is twenty paces across the yard. Inside, a grandmother and two children are shivering by a cold hearth.

choices.text: Run for the woodpile with an axe

ok.log: You make the woodpile, chop, load, and get back with an armful as the first wolf reaches the door. The hearth roars. The children cheer.

fail.deathCause: the wolves of the snowed-in inn
fail.log: They come from both sides. You get back inside with half an armful and the white wolf's teeth in your leg.

choices.text: Burn the inn's spare benches and tables

effects.log: The innkeeper weeps over his tables. They burn beautifully. The children sleep warm. Furniture can be bought.

choices.text: Pull everyone into one room and share the quilts

effects.log: Twelve people in one room under every quilt in the inn. Nobody is warm. Nobody freezes. The innkeeper tells terrible jokes all night.

events.text: The seventh night the wolves try the stable door. Inside are the inn's two horses and the travellers' mules: everything that gets anyone out of here when the snow stops. The white wolf is at the front, eyes like lamps.

choices.text: Hold the stable door with a torch and a spear

ok.log: You hold the door until dawn. The white wolf tries you three times and goes. When the sun comes up, the pack is gone with it.

fail.deathCause: the wolves of the snowed-in inn
fail.log: They break through the side boards. You save the horses, not yourself, and lie in the straw bleeding when the sun comes up.

choices.text: Set a fire in a barrel at the stable door

effects.log: Wolves hate fire more than they love horses. The barrel burns all night, fed with the last of the inn's oil. The pack circles and gives up.

choices.text: Let the mules out the back to draw the pack away

effects.log: It is a terrible choice. The mules run, the pack follows, the horses live. In spring you pay the muleteers for their beasts out of your own purse.

events.text: The herb-gatherers of the bamboo hills carry a stick to tap the path ahead. 'The green ones sleep on the branches at face height,' one says. 'Bamboo-coloured. You only see them when they see you.'

choices.text: Cut yourself a tapping stick

effects.log: You learn the rhythm: tap, look up, step. It feels foolish. The gatherers nod approvingly.

choices.text: Buy an antidote from the gatherers

effects.log: A little gourd of black paste that smells of rotten wood. 'Rub it in and run to a healer,' they say. 'It buys you half a day.'

choices.text: Laugh and go on

effects.log: The gatherers shrug. One of them, very old, has a hand with two fingers missing. You stop laughing.

events.text: Deep in the bamboo, ducking under a leaning stem, you find yourself nose to nose with a green viper coiled on the branch, mouth open, as still as the leaves. It is too close to step back from.

choices.text: Freeze, and breathe so slowly you do not move

ok.log: It stares into your eyes for a hundred heartbeats. Then it loses interest and flows up into the leaves. You sit down on the path.

fail.deathCause: a green bamboo viper's bite
fail.log: It strikes. A bite on the cheek like a hot nail. You stagger downhill to the herb village, half blind with the swelling.

choices.text: Swat it away with your hand

ok.log: Your hand is faster. The viper sails into the bamboo. You walk on with your heart going like a drum.

fail.deathCause: a green bamboo viper's bite
fail.log: It is faster. It bites your wrist and holds on. By the time you reach the herb village your arm is the colour of a plum.

choices.text: Tap the stem with your stick from below

effects.log: Tap. The viper unwinds and drops away into the leaf litter, offended. The gatherers' trick works.

choices.text: Sink down and crawl backward under the stem

effects.log: You go down on your knees in the leaf litter, slowly, slowly, and back away on all fours. Your knees are cut to pieces on the bamboo stubs. Your face is not.

events.text: In the herb village a child has been bitten by a green viper while picking mushrooms. The healer is away. The child's hand is swelling and the parents are wailing.

choices.text: Use the antidote paste you carry

effects.log: Black paste rubbed in, the hand bound, the child carried at a run to the healer in the next valley. The child lives. The parents name a pig after you.

choices.text: Keep the child still and carry them to the healer

effects.log: Still, low, quick. You carry the child through the bamboo in the dark, three hours. The healer says stillness saved the hand.

choices.text: Try to draw out the venom yourself

ok.log: You know enough to cut the cloth tight above the bite and keep the hand low. It is enough, until the healer comes.

fail.log: You do something the healer later calls well-meant and useless. The child lives anyway, but sick for a month.

events.arc: The Yellow Wind on the Western Road
events.text: A caravan bound west along the desert road. The old camel driver keeps looking at the horizon, which is a smudge of brown. 'Yellow wind,' he says. 'Two days, three. When it comes, lie down behind a camel and do not get up.'

choices.text: Ask how to survive it

effects.log: 'Cover the mouth, wet cloth. Tie yourself to the camel. Do not try to walk. People who walk are found in spring.' You remember every word.

choices.text: Buy a spare waterskin

effects.log: The water seller doubles the price when he hears about the wind. You pay it.

choices.text: Tell the caravan master to turn back

effects.log: The caravan master laughs. The silk must reach the western market by the moon. The camel driver does not laugh.

events.arc: The Yellow Wind on the Western Road
events.text: The yellow wind comes at noon: a wall of brown from the earth to the sky, and then you are inside it. You cannot see your hand. The sand is screaming. Someone is shouting for a lost child, somewhere very close.

choices.text: Let go of the rope and look for the child

ok.log: Your hand closes on a small sleeve in the brown dark. You crawl back along your own tracks to the camels and do not let go for two days.

fail.deathCause: the yellow wind on the western road
fail.log: You lose the child, the rope and the caravan. You lie in the sand for a day and a night until the camel driver finds you by luck.

choices.text: Shout, and keep shouting, from beside the camel

effects.log: You shout until your throat bleeds. The child follows your voice and falls against your legs. You tie the child to the camel with you.

choices.text: Lie down behind the camel as the old man said

effects.log: Wet cloth, the camel's warm flank, eyes shut. Two days of screaming wind. When it stops, the child is found under another camel, alive.

events.arc: The Yellow Wind on the Western Road
events.text: After the yellow wind, the caravan is scattered over ten li of new dunes. Three people are missing, and the water is low. The caravan master wants to leave before the heat of the day.

choices.text: Search the dunes at dawn

effects.log: You find two of them, half-buried and alive. The third is found by the camels, who smell water and walk straight to an old well nobody knew was there.

choices.text: Share your spare waterskin

effects.log: It gets the youngest driver through to the oasis. He tells everyone about it for the rest of his life.

choices.text: Follow the old camel driver's lead

effects.log: He walks the camels in a slow spiral. By noon all three are found. 'Desert hides things,' he says. 'It also gives them back, if you are patient.'

events.text: At the head of the great gorge, the boatmen are arguing. The river is high with spring melt and a whirlpool called the Dragon's Throat has opened below the third bend. Only one boatman will run it today, for triple fare.

choices.text: Wait for the water to fall

effects.log: Four days in a damp inn. On the fifth, the river drops and the Dragon's Throat closes. You pass it at a fair price.

choices.text: Pay triple and go

effects.log: The boatman is a tiny old woman with arms like ropes, who laughs at the river. You get in.

choices.text: Ask the boatmen how the whirlpool works

effects.log: 'It eats boats that fight it,' says one. 'Go into it sideways and let it spit you out.' The others say he is mad.

events.text: Below the third bend the river roars like an army. The boat spins. Ahead, the Dragon's Throat: a hole in the water as wide as a house, turning. A passenger in a fine robe panics, stands up, and the boat lurches toward it.

choices.text: Pull the panicking passenger down

ok.log: You drag the fine robe into the bottom of the boat. The boatwoman hits the whirlpool sideways and it spits you out into the calm, all of you soaked and alive.

fail.deathCause: the Dragon's Throat of the great gorge
fail.log: The passenger fights you and you both go over the side into the white water. You come up a li downstream, against a rock, battered.

choices.text: Grab an oar and do what the boatwoman shouts

effects.log: She shouts. You row. She shouts the other way. You row. The boat slides sideways into the Throat and out of it like a pip from a fruit.

choices.text: Go in sideways, as the boatmen said

effects.log: You shout it to the boatwoman: sideways. She grins and does it. The Dragon's Throat spits the boat out like a cherry stone.

events.text: The fine-robed passenger from the gorge is a salt official, it turns out, and has sent a servant to find you with a letter. Inside, an invitation, and a request: the official wants to pay for a stone marker at the Dragon's Throat.

choices.text: Help carve the warning on the marker

effects.log: DO NOT STAND, in characters as tall as a person, on the rock at the third bend. Boatmen laugh at it for years and then stop laughing, because nobody drowns there any more.

choices.text: Suggest the money go to the boatwoman

effects.log: The official is puzzled and then pays her a pension. She buys a new boat with it and runs the gorge until she is ninety.

choices.text: Accept the official's thanks, and a purse

effects.log: A heavy purse and a promise of a favour. You keep the purse and save the favour.

events.text: No rain for two months. The hills are the colour of straw. At a shrine on the ridge, an old caretaker keeps sweeping pine needles off the path. 'One spark,' he says, 'and the whole mountain goes.'

choices.text: Help him clear a firebreak around the shrine

effects.log: Two days of raking needles into a wide bare ring. The caretaker says it is the first time anyone has helped. Your hands are black with resin.

choices.text: Ask which way the wind blows in the afternoon

effects.log: 'Up the valley, always. A fire goes up a hill like a cat up a tree.' He points: never be above a fire.

choices.text: Go on through the hills

effects.log: You camp on the ridge that night without a fire, and smell smoke on the wind, far off.

events.text: The afternoon wind brings smoke. Below you on the slope, the dry grass is burning in a long orange line, racing uphill toward the ridge where you stand. It is moving faster than a man can run.

choices.text: Run sideways along the slope, not up

effects.log: Across the hill, not up it. The fire roars past below you and goes up into the pines. You sit on bare rock, coughing, watching the mountain burn.

choices.text: Run for the top of the ridge

ok.log: You make the ridge and go over it, down the other side, with the fire's breath on your back. Your eyebrows are gone.

fail.deathCause: the fire on the dry hills
fail.log: The fire is faster. You fall in the grass with the heat on your back and only a stream saves you. You lie in it until the fire is past.

choices.text: Run to the cleared ring around the shrine

effects.log: Bare earth, a wide ring. The fire splits around it like water round a stone. You and the caretaker crouch by the shrine, breathing through wet cloths.

events.text: The hills are black. The village below them lost its barns but no lives, because the caretaker rang the shrine bell. Now the caretaker is ill from the smoke, and the village has nothing for the winter.

choices.text: Help rebuild the barns

effects.log: A month of carrying timber. The village sends you off with a feast it cannot afford, and you cannot refuse.

choices.text: Bring the caretaker medicine from the town

effects.log: The caretaker recovers, sweeping again by spring. The ring around the shrine is wider now. He makes you rake it once more, for luck.

choices.text: Plant the first seedlings on the black slope

effects.log: Pine and oak, in rows. You will not see them grown. Somebody will.

events.arc: The Road Crew Under the Cliff
events.text: The county is cutting a new road under a cliff of rotten yellow rock. The foreman pays well and fast, because nobody wants the work. Every few hours a pebble comes down from the top and bounces off the road with a sound like a dropped coin.

choices.text: Take the work, and listen to the pebbles

effects.log: You learn the sound. One pebble is nothing. Three together means run. The old hands taught you, and they are still alive.

choices.text: Take the work, and ask for the safe end

effects.log: The foreman gives you the end of the cut nearest the river, laughing at your caution. The pay is a little less.

choices.text: Tell the foreman the cliff is coming down

effects.log: The foreman says the cliff has been coming down for a thousand years and has not managed it yet. He offers you double to stay.

events.arc: The Road Crew Under the Cliff
events.text: Afternoon, after a night of rain. Three pebbles come down together, then a handful of gravel, then a sound from the top of the cliff like a giant clearing its throat. The crew below has not heard it over their hammers.

choices.text: Shout and run for the river end, waving everyone after you

effects.log: You run, shouting. Most of the crew follow. Behind you the cliff face slides down onto the road with a roar that you feel in your teeth. When the dust clears, everyone is counted.

choices.text: Go back for the old stonecutter who is half deaf

ok.log: You grab the old man under the arms and drag him into the river as the cliff comes down where he was sitting. You both come up spluttering, alive.

fail.deathCause: a rockfall under the yellow cliff
fail.log: You reach him and the rocks reach you both. You dig yourselves out an hour later, broken in places, but breathing.

choices.text: You heard it first: run before the throat-clearing ends

effects.log: Three pebbles, then gravel: you are running before the others look up, and your shout is enough. Nobody is under the cliff when it comes.

events.arc: The Road Crew Under the Cliff
events.text: The county magistrate's clerk comes to see the fallen cliff and asks who gave the warning. The foreman points at you, and does not look at you while he does it.

choices.text: Ask the clerk to make the road go round

effects.log: The clerk, to everyone's surprise, writes it down. Two years later the road goes round the cliff along the river. It is longer and nobody dies building it.

choices.text: Ask the clerk for the crew's back pay

effects.log: The foreman hid it. The clerk finds it. Every man and woman of the crew is paid. They buy you dinner for a week.

choices.text: Say nothing and go back to work

effects.log: There is a lot of rubble to move. You move it. The foreman gives you the safe end of the cut for good.

events.text: A beekeeper in the hills warns travellers off the short path through the next valley. 'Giant hornets,' she says, and holds up her thumb. 'Like that. Their nest is in a hollow tree by the path. Three stings drop a horse.'

choices.text: Take the long path round

effects.log: It costs you a day. On the ridge you can hear the valley humming like a struck bell.

choices.text: Ask how to pass if you must

effects.log: 'At night, when they sleep. Smoke. And never, ever run past the nest.' She gives you a smoking pot of rags on a string.

choices.text: Ask if she needs the nest gone

effects.log: She looks at you a long time. 'My bees are dying. Their nest eats my hives.' She does not ask. She does not have to.

events.text: The short path, at dusk, against advice or for the beekeeper's sake. The hollow tree is ahead, humming. A single hornet, as long as your thumb, hangs in the air in front of your face, looking at you. It is a scout.

choices.text: Run past the nest before the rest come

ok.log: You are past the tree in four strides and down the valley before the swarm is up. Behind you the humming turns to a roar, and fades.

fail.deathCause: the hornets of the valley
fail.log: The swarm comes out like smoke. You are stung on the neck and arms before you reach the stream and go under. You lie in the water, burning.

choices.text: Stand still and let the scout lose interest

effects.log: You stand like a post. The hornet circles your head three times, lands on your cheek, and leaves. You back away the way you came and take the long path.

choices.text: Swing the smoking pot and walk past slowly

effects.log: The smoke rolls over the hollow tree. The humming drops to a drowsy mutter. You walk past at a slow, steady pace, every muscle screaming to run.

events.text: The beekeeper's hives are dying. The hornet nest is the size of a water jar now. She has a plan: at midnight, a sack over the hollow, smoke, and fire. Someone has to hold the sack.

choices.text: Hold the sack over the hollow

ok.log: The sack goes on, the smoke goes in, the hollow is plugged with burning rags. In the morning there is silence. Her bees are humming again by the summer.

fail.deathCause: the hornets of the valley
fail.log: The sack tears. A dozen hornets get out and find you. You live, swollen, feverish, in her house for a week.

choices.text: Light the fire from a distance with a long pole

effects.log: Slower, safer, and it works. The beekeeper calls you a coward, kindly, and gives you a jar of honey.

choices.text: Move her hives to the next valley instead

effects.log: Three nights of carrying humming hives on a pole. The bees are saved. The hornets keep their tree. Everyone is happy except your shoulders.

events.text: In the marsh country the locals will not travel in fog. 'Ghost lights,' an old woman at the inn says. 'Little lanterns out in the reeds. Follow them and you walk into the deep water. The dead like company.'

choices.text: Laugh it off

effects.log: The old woman shrugs. 'Then laugh in the reeds,' she says, 'and see who laughs back.'

choices.text: Ask what the lights really are

effects.log: 'Marsh gas,' says the innkeeper's son. 'Burning. Or the dead.' He grins. 'The water is deep either way.'

choices.text: Buy a long pole to test the ground

effects.log: A bamboo pole as long as two people. The innkeeper's son says you will look ridiculous. You will look alive.

events.text: The fog comes down on the marsh causeway in the afternoon, so thick you cannot see your feet. Out in the reeds, a little light bobs and glows, warm, like a lamp in a window, and moves away as if leading you home.

choices.text: Follow the light: it might be a house

ok.log: It leads you along a firm ridge of earth to a fisherman's hut. The fisherman, carrying a lantern, is very surprised to see you.

fail.deathCause: the deep water under the marsh fog
fail.log: The ground gives under you and black water closes over your head. You come up tangled in reeds and claw your way back to the causeway.

choices.text: Sit down on the causeway and wait for the fog to lift

effects.log: A cold, wet night on the stones. At dawn the fog lifts. The light was over a pool so deep the reeds around it are black.

choices.text: Probe every step with the long pole

effects.log: Step, probe, step. Twice the pole goes down into nothing where the ground looked solid. You reach the far side at midnight, soaked to the knees, laughing at the dark.

events.text: In the fishing village at the marsh's edge, a child has gone out after the ghost lights in the fog and not come back. The parents are on the causeway, calling. The fog is rolling in again.

choices.text: Ring the village gong, steady, all night

effects.log: A gong is a lamp for ears. You strike it once every ten breaths, all night. Near dawn a small voice calls back from the reeds, following the sound home.

choices.text: Wade into the reeds after the child

ok.log: You find the child clinging to a reed bank, waist-deep, crying. You carry the child back on your shoulders. The village cheers.

fail.deathCause: the deep water under the marsh fog
fail.log: You find the child, and lose the causeway. You hold the child above the water all night until the fog lifts.

choices.text: Light a line of fires along the causeway

effects.log: Every family brings a brazier. A line of real fires, not ghost ones. The child sees them and walks out along the firm ground, by itself, proud.

events.arc: The Northern Pass in the Thaw
events.text: At the foot of the northern pass the herders are waiting for the thaw to finish. 'The snow is rotten,' an old herder says, pointing at the slopes above the pass road. 'When it hangs like a wet sheet, it falls. Listen for the crack. Then you have three breaths.'

choices.text: Wait with the herders until the slopes are bare

effects.log: Nine days of mutton and dice. On the tenth day the snow slides down on its own in the night with a sound like thunder. The road is clear after.

choices.text: Ask what to do in the three breaths

effects.log: 'Run sideways. Throw off your pack. If it takes you, swim. Spit, and dig the way the spit falls.' The old herder looks at you. 'Spit falls down. Dig the other way.'

choices.text: Go now, before the price of mutton ruins you

effects.log: The herders shake their heads as you go up. One of them, young, comes after you, because someone has to know where to dig.

events.arc: The Northern Pass in the Thaw
events.text: Halfway up the pass, in the noon sun, the slope above you makes a sound like a bone breaking. A line has opened across the snow. The whole white face of the mountain begins, very slowly, to move.

choices.text: Run sideways, as the herder said

effects.log: Sideways, not down. You throw off your pack and run across the slope with the mountain coming down behind you. It passes, roaring, a spear's length away.

choices.text: Race the snow down the road

ok.log: You run faster than you have ever run. The snow cloud overtakes you and passes, and you are still on your feet, white as a ghost, alive.

fail.deathCause: an avalanche on the northern pass
fail.log: It catches you and you are under. White, silent, upside down. You spit, and dig the other way, and break out into the air an hour later.

choices.text: Spit, and dig the other way

effects.log: It takes you. In the white dark you remember the old herder. Spit falls. You dig upward, slowly, until there is light. You come out half frozen and laughing at the sky.

choices.text: Throw yourself flat behind a boulder

effects.log: You press your face into the snow behind a rock the size of a house. The mountain goes over you like a river over a stone, and then it is quiet. You dig out bruised, and deaf in one ear for a week.

events.arc: The Northern Pass in the Thaw
events.text: The young herder who followed you up the pass is missing under the avalanche. There is a mitten on the snow, near the edge of the slide. The slope above still hangs, wet and heavy.

choices.text: Dig for the herder under the hanging slope

ok.log: You dig with your hands until they bleed, and find a face, and a breath. You drag the herder out and down the road before the second slide.

fail.deathCause: an avalanche on the northern pass
fail.log: The second slide comes while you are digging. You are both buried. You both live, by luck, and dig each other out.

choices.text: Run back down for the herders and their poles

effects.log: An hour down, an hour up. The herders probe the snow in a line. They find the young one under a drift, cold but breathing.

choices.text: Probe from the edge with a long branch

effects.log: You work from the safe side, inch by inch, and feel the branch hit something soft. You dig sideways to it. The herder is alive, and grinning, and missing a mitten.

events.arc: The Northern Pass in the Thaw
events.text: Years later, at the foot of the northern pass, the herders have built a stone hut on the safe side with a bell and a line of long poles leaning against it. The young herder you dug out is the old herder now.

choices.text: Ring the bell for luck

effects.log: The bell echoes up the pass. Somewhere above, a little snow slides off a ledge. The herders all laugh. It is a good omen, they decide.

choices.text: Sit with the herder and remember

effects.log: Mutton, dice, and the story told again, both of you correcting each other on every detail. You are both certain you were braver than the other.

choices.text: Teach the travellers there what the old herder taught you

effects.log: Three breaths. Run sideways. Spit, and dig the other way. A merchant writes it down. It is on the hut door now.

events.text: In the berry season the mountain villagers go up in groups and sing as they pick. 'Bears do not like singing,' says an old picker. 'And a bear that is surprised is a bear that fights. Always let it hear you coming.'

choices.text: Go up with the singing pickers

effects.log: You sing badly and pick well. Twice you hear something large moving away through the bushes, uninterested. The old picker nods at you.

choices.text: Go up alone, quietly, to find the best bushes

effects.log: You find the best bushes. You also find bear droppings full of berry seeds, still warm. You go back down, rather fast.

choices.text: Ask what to do if you meet one

effects.log: 'Stand tall. Talk to it, low, like a person. Back away. Never run. A bear runs faster than a horse downhill.'

events.text: You come round a boulder into a berry clearing and there is a black bear, ten steps away, eating from a bush with two cubs behind it. It rises on its hind legs, taller than you, and looks at you. The cubs squeal.

choices.text: Stand tall, talk low, and back away

effects.log: 'Easy. Easy, mother. I am going.' Step by step, back round the boulder. The bear drops to four legs, huffs once, and goes back to its berries.

choices.text: Run for it

ok.log: You run downhill faster than you knew you could. The bear chases a little, for form, then goes back to its cubs.

fail.deathCause: a mother bear in berry season
fail.log: It is faster. It knocks you down and stands over you, roaring, and then, satisfied, leaves you in the berries with your back torn open.

choices.text: Lie flat on the ground, very still

effects.log: You lie in the berries with your face down. The bear comes and sniffs your neck, huffs hot breath on you, and goes away with its cubs. You lie there a long time afterward.

choices.text: Throw your basket of berries toward it and back off

effects.log: The bear considers the berries, considers you, and chooses the berries. You walk away with nothing and everything.

events.text: The village is in an uproar. A young bear has come down to the village at night, raiding the beehives and the grain. The hunters want to kill it. The old picker says it is one of the cubs from the clearing, grown, and hungry.

choices.text: Help the villagers guard their hives with drums

effects.log: Every night, drums at the hives. The young bear comes, hears them, and goes away. After a week it stops coming.

choices.text: Lead the bear away with a trail of honeycomb

effects.log: A honeycomb trail up the mountain, a long way, at dawn. The young bear follows it into the high valley. It does not come back.

choices.text: Join the hunters

ok.log: The hunt is short. The village has meat for winter and a bearskin for the headman's floor. The old picker does not speak to you again.

fail.deathCause: a young bear raiding the village
fail.log: The young bear is quicker than any of you. You take its claws across the arm, and it escapes up the mountain.

events.text: The tide road across the salt marsh is only safe at low water, and only on the line of old stakes. A boy selling dried fish at the marsh edge says his uncle walked off the stakes in the mist last year, and the mud took him to the waist, and then the tide came in.

choices.text: Ask the boy when the tide turns

effects.log: 'When the gulls go quiet,' he says. 'Then you have an hour, not more.' He sells you a fish for the advice.

choices.text: Wait for a guide

effects.log: A salt carrier with two baskets goes across every day. You follow her, stake to stake, never talking. She charges you a copper.

choices.text: Cross now, quickly

effects.log: You cross with the water low and the stakes clear. Halfway, you look down and see a straw hat half-sunk in the mud a little off the line. You do not stop.

events.text: Crossing the salt marsh, a step off the line of stakes in the mist, the ground turns to porridge under you. You are in to the knees, then the thighs. The gulls have gone quiet. Out in the grey, you can hear the sea coming back.

choices.text: Lie back flat on the mud and spread your arms

effects.log: Every instinct screams. You lie back anyway. The mud lets go of your legs, slowly, and you roll and crawl to the stake line on your belly like a seal.

choices.text: Pull your legs free by force

ok.log: You heave and the mud gives with a great sucking noise. You leave your boots behind and run for the stakes barefoot as the water rises.

fail.deathCause: the mud and the tide of the salt marsh
fail.log: The harder you pull the deeper you go. The tide is at your chest when you finally drag yourself onto a stake and hang there until low water.

choices.text: Shout for the salt carrier

effects.log: You hear her before you see her, cursing. She throws you a basket strap and hauls you out with the strength of thirty years of salt.

events.text: The marsh village, years on. The line of stakes is rotting and the headman cannot pay for new ones. The salt carrier, very old now, still crosses every day.

choices.text: Pay for a new line of stakes

effects.log: Tall ones, painted red at the top, so you can see them in the mist. The salt carrier walks across them the first day and says they are much too bright.

choices.text: Help drive the new stakes in yourself

effects.log: A month of low tides, a mallet and a lot of mud. The red-topped stakes stand in a line across the marsh like a row of herons.

choices.text: Teach the children the gull rule

effects.log: When the gulls go quiet, you have an hour. The village children shout it at every traveller like a song.

events.text: On the coast, the fishing boats are not going out though the sea is flat and the sky is clear. The old fishermen are looking at a long swell rolling in from the south, slow and greasy, and at the birds flying inland. 'Typhoon,' one says. 'Two days. Tie down what you love.'

choices.text: Help the fishermen haul their boats up the beach

effects.log: Twenty boats, a hundred people, ropes, rollers and song. By evening every boat is above the tide line and lashed to stakes.

choices.text: Ask where people shelter

effects.log: 'The stone temple on the headland. It has stood through forty typhoons.' The old fisherman says it like a prayer.

choices.text: Take the next boat out before it comes

effects.log: No boat will take you. A merchant ship's captain laughs at the fishermen and sails anyway. You do not get on it.

events.text: The typhoon comes at night. The wind screams like a living thing. A roof flies past in the dark. Somewhere down by the harbour someone is screaming for help, and the sea is coming over the harbour wall.

choices.text: Go down to the harbour

ok.log: A family clinging to a broken roof in the water. You get them out one by one along a rope tied to the temple gate. Then you collapse.

fail.deathCause: the typhoon on the coast
fail.log: A wave takes you off the harbour wall. You are thrown against the boats and dragged out half drowned by the fishermen.

choices.text: Shelter in the stone temple and keep the door

effects.log: All night you hold the temple door against the wind with ten others. Everyone who comes, you let in. By dawn there are two hundred people in a temple built for fifty.

choices.text: Tie a rope from your house to the next, and wait

effects.log: A rope across the lane, so nobody is blown away crossing it. The neighbours use it all night. You do not sleep.

choices.text: Hold on and wait for dawn

effects.log: You lie under a table with your arms over your head while the house shakes. The roof goes at midnight. You live.

events.text: Dawn after the typhoon. The village is half gone. The boats you hauled up the beach are mostly whole. The merchant ship that sailed out is on the rocks across the bay, broken, with people still on it.

choices.text: Take a fishing boat out to the wreck

effects.log: The fishermen say no, then yes, then all come with you. Eleven sailors off the rocks by noon. The merchant captain is not among them.

choices.text: Organise the clearing of the lanes

effects.log: A thousand broken roof tiles, a hundred fallen trees, one terrified goat on a roof. By the end of the week the village has paths again.

choices.text: Help the healers at the temple

effects.log: Broken arms, cuts, a baby born in the middle of it all. You carry water all day. The baby is named after the typhoon, which is unlucky, so they change it to yours.

events.text: The fishing village has rebuilt. At the harbour there is a new thing: a tall pole with a black flag, to be raised when the long greasy swell comes and the birds fly inland. The old fishermen say you put the idea in their heads.

choices.text: Raise the flag the first time it is needed

effects.log: The swell comes. You raise it. Every boat stays in. That night a storm sweeps the coast and no one in the village is lost.

choices.text: Teach the children to read the swell

effects.log: Slow, greasy, from the south. Birds flying inland. The children know it now like their own names.

choices.text: Leave the village a little better and go

effects.log: You leave a purse for the temple roof. The headland temple, which has stood through forty-one typhoons, will stand through more.

events.text: In the market town under Black Wind Ridge, merchants travel in groups of thirty and still come back short. The stronghold on the ridge takes a tithe from every road. A tea seller whispers that the chief, One-Eyed Zhao, has started taking people as well as goods, for ransom.

choices.text: Listen to everything the tea seller knows

effects.log: Three roads, two passes, one gorge path nobody watches because it is too steep. Zhao drinks every night. Zhao is afraid of the magistrate's new captain.

choices.text: Join a merchant group as a guard

effects.log: Thirty merchants, six guards, a lot of bad jokes. You cross under the ridge and nothing happens. The pay is good. You do not believe it will last.

choices.text: Avoid the ridge entirely

effects.log: A long road round the province. You hear later that the next caravan through the pass lost everything, including the guards' boots.

events.text: On the pass road under Black Wind Ridge, a horn blows. Bandits in black scarves come down the slope on both sides, forty of them, shouting. The merchants freeze. The caravan master looks at you: fight, pay, or run.

choices.text: Hold the narrow part of the road

ok.log: You hold a gap between two rocks while the merchants turn the carts. The bandits break against you three times and fall back. The caravan escapes.

fail.deathCause: the bandits of Black Wind Ridge
fail.log: There are too many. You go down under clubs and wake tied over a mule, on your way up to the stronghold.

choices.text: Pay the toll and save the people

effects.log: The merchants weep over their silk. Nobody is hurt. A black-scarfed lieutenant counts the toll and looks at you a long time, memorising your face.

choices.text: Lead the carts down the steep gorge path

effects.log: The tea seller's path. Too steep for horses. The carts nearly go over twice. The bandits come down on an empty road and howl at the gorge.

events.text: Word comes down from the ridge: One-Eyed Zhao has taken the magistrate's young nephew for ransom, and will send back a finger every three days until paid. The magistrate's captain is gathering men, too few. The captain asks for you.

choices.text: Go up the ridge with the captain's men

ok.log: A dawn attack on the stronghold gate. Smoke, shouting, a burning watchtower. The nephew is found in a storeroom, scared and whole.

fail.deathCause: the bandits of Black Wind Ridge
fail.log: The gate holds. The captain's men are driven back down the ridge, and you with an arrow in the leg.

choices.text: Climb the gorge path alone at night and find the boy

effects.log: Up the steep path in the dark, over the back wall. A storeroom lock. A boy crying in the dark. You carry him down the gorge on your back.

choices.text: Help the captain plan instead

effects.log: You draw the ridge, the roads, the gate. The captain listens. The attack is smaller and smarter. It frees the nephew and loses no one. You stay at the bottom with the horses.

events.text: One-Eyed Zhao has come down from the ridge alone, wounded, under a white flag, and asks to talk to you. The stronghold has fallen to a younger, crueller lieutenant. Zhao says the new chief will burn the market town at the full moon.

choices.text: Believe Zhao, and warn the town

effects.log: The town builds barricades at the gate. At the full moon the new chief comes down with torches and finds the town ready. They turn back. Zhao is gone in the night.

choices.text: Hand Zhao over to the magistrate

effects.log: Zhao goes quietly, saying nothing. The magistrate, warned by you of the full moon anyway, sends the captain to wait in the hills.

choices.text: Go up the ridge with Zhao to end it

roll.foeName: the new chief of Black Wind

ok.log: You and the old chief walk into the stronghold together. The young chief's men see Zhao's face and half of them put down their weapons. It ends in an hour.

fail.deathCause: the new chief of Black Wind Ridge
fail.log: The young chief is ready. You fight your way out with Zhao dying behind you.

events.text: Black Wind Ridge is quiet. The stronghold is a ruin with goats in it. In the market town under the ridge, a tea seller who used to whisper now speaks out loud, and the caravans go over the pass in groups of three.

choices.text: Climb up to the ruined stronghold once more

effects.log: Goats, wild flowers, the burned gate. From the top you can see the three roads, all of them busy. You sit for a long time.

choices.text: Drink tea with the old tea seller

effects.log: The tea seller tells you the story of Black Wind Ridge. You are in it. It is much braver than it was. You do not correct anything.

choices.text: Put up a shrine on the pass for the ones who did not make it

effects.log: A little stone shrine and a stick of incense. Caravans stop there now, to leave a coin. The coins go to the widows in town.

events.text: In a river town, three families have fallen sick in a week with cramps and green faces. The healer blames bad pork. You notice they all live on the same lane, and all draw water from the same well.

choices.text: Tell the healer about the well

effects.log: The healer is offended, then thoughtful, then has the well roped off. Two more families fall sick the next day, on the other side of town. They drank from a different well.

choices.text: Watch the well at night

effects.log: At midnight a figure in a dark hood comes to the well, pauses, and goes. Too dark to see a face. You notice the figure limps.

choices.text: Carry water from the river for the sick families

effects.log: Buckets from the river, boiled. The sick families recover slowly. Their neighbours start doing the same.

events.text: Another well, another lane, sick people in every house. The town is panicking, blaming strangers. A crowd has seized a foreign herb seller at the market and is shouting for a rope.

choices.text: Stand between the crowd and the herb seller

effects.log: A hundred angry faces. You do not move. You talk: three wells, all poisoned at night, all in different lanes. The herb seller has been in the market all week. The crowd wavers, then goes.

choices.text: Pull the herb seller out and run

ok.log: Over a wall, down an alley, into the river reeds. The crowd loses you both. The herb seller presses a little bag of medicine into your hand.

fail.deathCause: an angry crowd in the river town
fail.log: The crowd catches you both at the river. Stones and fists. You shield the herb seller until the watchmen come.

choices.text: Run for the town watch

effects.log: The watchmen come, outnumbered, and make the crowd hand the herb seller over to them. It is not justice. It is a cell instead of a rope.

events.text: The limping figure, the hooded one. You follow the limp through the town's back lanes to a house behind the temple: the house of the town's own well-digger, who lost the contract for the new wells last spring.

choices.text: Confront the well-digger at the door

ok.log: The well-digger draws a knife and drops it when you catch the wrist. A bag of grey powder spills on the step. The watch is called.

fail.deathCause: a poisoner's powder in the river town
fail.log: The well-digger throws the powder in your face. Your eyes burn and your throat closes. You get the knife away, half blind, before you fall.

choices.text: Bring the magistrate's men quietly to the house

effects.log: They search it at dawn. A sack of grey powder, wet from the well. The well-digger is taken without a fight, weeping.

choices.text: Leave a note for the magistrate and leave town

effects.log: You leave a note. You do not know if anyone reads it. The poisonings stop the next week. You never find out why.

events.text: The wells of the river town are being cleaned: dozens of men with buckets, the bottoms scraped, fresh stones laid. The herb seller the crowd nearly hanged is supervising the cleaning, by the magistrate's order.

choices.text: Help clean the wells

effects.log: Cold mud to the knees, all day. The herb seller teaches you which powders turn green in water. It is good knowledge. You hope never to need it again.

choices.text: Ask what will happen to the well-digger

effects.log: Exile, the magistrate says, to the northern salt pans. The herb seller asked for mercy. The town did not, but the magistrate listened.

choices.text: Drink the first cup from the clean well

effects.log: In front of the whole town, you drink. It is cold and tastes of stone. The town cheers and lines up. Fear, it seems, can also be poured out.

events.arc: The Guide Who Knew Too Little
events.text: A cheerful guide offers to lead you over the mountains by a shortcut, cheap. He knows the road like his own hand, he says. When you ask the name of the pass, he gives a different name than he gave the merchant beside you an hour ago.

choices.text: Hire him anyway, but watch him

effects.log: He walks fast and talks a lot. Twice he looks back down the trail as if he expected someone to be following. You keep your hand near your blade.

choices.text: Ask the innkeeper about him

effects.log: The innkeeper goes quiet, then says: 'Travellers who hire him do not come back through here.' Then pretends he said nothing.

choices.text: Refuse and take the main road

effects.log: Slower, dull, safe. At the next town you see the cheerful guide's face on a magistrate's poster, with a price under it.

events.arc: The Guide Who Knew Too Little
events.text: High on the shortcut, at a narrow ledge above a drop, the guide stops and whistles. Three men step out from behind the rocks ahead, armed, blocking the ledge. The guide steps back behind you, smiling.

choices.text: Fight on the ledge

ok.log: The ledge is narrow and only one can come at you at a time. One, two, three. The guide runs.

fail.deathCause: robbers on a mountain ledge
fail.log: One of them gets past your guard and you go off the edge, catching a root. They take your pack and leave you hanging there.

choices.text: Throw them your purse and step back

effects.log: The purse goes over to them. They count it, laugh, and let you go back down the way you came. The guide waves.

choices.text: Seize the guide before he can run

effects.log: You were watching him. You grab the guide by the collar before the robbers move, and hold him over the edge. They put their weapons down.

events.arc: The Guide Who Knew Too Little
events.text: In a town on the far side of the mountains, the cheerful guide is sitting in a teahouse, cheerful as ever, talking to a young couple with heavy packs about a shortcut over the mountains.

choices.text: Sit down at their table and tell the couple your story

effects.log: The guide stops smiling. The couple gets up and leaves. The guide leaves a moment later, very fast, without paying.

choices.text: Drag the guide to the magistrate

ok.log: The guide fights like a cat and loses. The magistrate already has a poster. There is a reward.

fail.deathCause: the guide's friends in a teahouse brawl
fail.log: The guide's friends are in the teahouse too. You end up in the street, beaten, and the guide is gone.

choices.text: Tell the magistrate where the guide drinks

effects.log: The magistrate's men come the next day. The guide is taken from his teahouse table, still talking.

events.text: A lonely inn on the forest road, very clean, very cheap. The innkeeper's wife pours you a cup of tea so sweet you can taste honey and something under the honey, bitter as almond. The other guests are already asleep at their tables.

choices.text: Pretend to drink, and pour it in your sleeve

effects.log: Your sleeve is sticky and you smell of almonds. You lean on the table, eyes half shut, and watch the innkeeper's wife watch you.

choices.text: Drink it; you are tired

ok.log: It is only very sweet tea. You sleep well. In the morning the other guests are gone, and so is your purse, and you are only glad you are alive.

fail.deathCause: drugged tea at a black inn
fail.log: Something in the honey stops your heart for a moment. You wake in a ditch behind the inn, robbed, freezing, alive by a hair.

choices.text: Leave the cup and go on in the dark

effects.log: The forest road at night is no friend. But by midnight you reach a charcoal burner's hut, and the burner, told of the inn, swears.

events.text: At the black inn, midnight. The innkeeper and two big sons come out of the kitchen with ropes and a lamp, and start going through the sleeping guests' packs. One of the guests is a young woman travelling with an old servant.

choices.text: Fight them in the dark

ok.log: They expected sleeping guests. You are not sleeping. The sons go down, the innkeeper runs into the forest. The guests wake to find the robbers tied up.

fail.deathCause: the robbers of the black inn
fail.log: The innkeeper hits you with a stool from behind. You fight on the floor, half stunned, until the guests start to wake and the robbers flee.

choices.text: Splash cold water on the sleepers to wake them

effects.log: Guest after guest, choking, waking. Five awake people with chairs are too many for three robbers. The innkeeper and the sons run.

choices.text: Slip out and run for the charcoal burners

effects.log: The burners come with axes and torches. By the time they arrive the inn is empty and the guests are robbed, but alive.

events.text: The black inn is shut. But a guest from that night, the old servant, finds you on the road and says the innkeeper's wife has opened another inn, two valleys over, very clean, very cheap, with very sweet tea.

choices.text: Warn every traveller you meet on the road

effects.log: For a month you tell everyone: do not drink sweet tea in clean cheap inns. Travellers think you are mad. The new inn has no customers.

choices.text: Go and close it yourself

ok.log: The innkeeper's wife sees your face at the door and drops the teapot. You hand her to the county magistrate in the morning.

fail.deathCause: the robbers of the black inn
fail.log: She has new sons, it seems. They are waiting for you. You get away bloodied.

choices.text: Tell the county magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate sends six constables in plain clothes to drink tea at the new inn. They are very brave about it. The tea is not drunk. The inn is shut.

events.text: A new inn on the forest road, where the black inn was: owned by the charcoal burners. It is dirty and expensive and the tea is terrible. Travellers love it. Nobody has ever been robbed there.

choices.text: Stay the night and drink the terrible tea

effects.log: It is the worst tea you have ever tasted. You sleep like a stone. In the morning your purse is exactly where you left it.

choices.text: Pay the burners for a sign

effects.log: THE TEA IS BAD BUT HONEST, the sign says. Travellers laugh at it. Then they stop, and read it twice, and come in.

choices.text: Ask the burners what happened to the old inn's sons

effects.log: One is in the salt pans. One is a charcoal burner now, working for them, very quiet, very hard. People change, the burners say. Sometimes.

events.arc: The Press-Gang on the Ferry Road
events.text: At the ferry landing there is a notice: the garrison needs men for the frontier. Under it, soldiers are 'helping' travellers into a holding pen. Anyone without papers or silver goes north in chains.

choices.text: Show your papers, if you have them

effects.log: The sergeant reads them upside down, sneers, and lets you pass. Behind you, a farm boy without papers is pulled into the pen.

choices.text: Pay the sergeant to look the other way

effects.log: Silver changes hands. The sergeant looks at the river very hard while you get on the ferry.

choices.text: Wait in the reeds for the soldiers to leave

effects.log: They leave at dusk with twenty men roped together. You cross at night with a fisherman, both of you silent.

events.arc: The Press-Gang on the Ferry Road
events.text: On the north road, the press-gang's column has stopped for the night in a barn. Twenty roped men. Four soldiers, two asleep. The farm boy from the ferry landing is crying in his sleep.

choices.text: Cut the ropes and fight the guards

ok.log: Two guards down, two running. Twenty men scatter into the night like quail. The farm boy goes home.

fail.deathCause: the press-gang on the north road
fail.log: The guards are awake after all. You are beaten and roped with the others.

choices.text: Cut the ropes quietly and slip away

effects.log: One knife, twenty ropes, no noise. By dawn the barn is empty and the guards are blaming each other.

choices.text: Leave a knife where the farm boy can reach it

effects.log: In the morning the barn is half empty. The ones who were brave enough went. You do not know if the boy was one of them.

events.arc: The Press-Gang on the Ferry Road
events.text: Back at the ferry landing, years later, the farm boy is a man with a farm, and the press-gang notice is torn and rotting. He sees you and drops his hoe.

choices.text: Let him thank you

effects.log: He takes you home and his whole family bows. Three children. A buffalo. A future that would not exist. You eat with them and leave before you can be thanked again.

choices.text: Ask if the gangs still come

effects.log: 'Not since the new magistrate.' He grins. 'Someone wrote to him about a barn on the north road.'

choices.text: Tear the old notice down

effects.log: You tear it off the post. He helps. Children come to watch. It is a small thing. It feels large.

events.text: A dying tomb robber in a roadside temple presses a map into your hands: a general's tomb in the hills, its gate, its corridors, three red marks. 'Traps,' he whispers. 'Arrows. Sand. The floor that turns. My brothers did not listen.'

choices.text: Learn the three red marks by heart

effects.log: Arrows at the first door. Sand in the second corridor. The turning floor before the coffin. You memorise them like a prayer.

choices.text: Burn the map; the dead should rest

effects.log: The robber laughs weakly. 'Then you are smarter than my brothers.' The map burns. You are a little sorry.

choices.text: Ask why he went in

effects.log: 'Gold,' he says. 'And because my father went in, and came out with one coin, and was never happy again.' He dies before morning.

events.text: The general's tomb. Behind the cracked gate, a corridor of stone soldiers. The robbers have been here: one lies in the dust with an old bronze arrow in the shoulder. He is alive and begging for help. Ahead, the floor is scattered with fresh sand from a crack in the ceiling.

choices.text: Carry the wounded robber out first

effects.log: You drag him out into the daylight and bind the wound. He is one of the dying man's brothers. He weeps when you tell him.

choices.text: Go on past the sand before the ceiling opens

ok.log: You run across as the ceiling groans, and the sand pours down behind you like a waterfall, sealing the way back. Ahead, the coffin chamber.

fail.deathCause: the sand trap in the general's tomb
fail.log: The ceiling opens on you. Sand to the waist, to the chest. You dig out with your hands over an hour and crawl back to the gate.

choices.text: Walk the edges where the map says, slowly

effects.log: The robber's map. Left wall, three steps, right wall. The ceiling does not move. You reach the coffin chamber without a grain of sand on you.

events.text: The coffin chamber. A stone coffin, a painted ceiling of stars, and in front of it a floor of square tiles. On the coffin lid, the general's sword, untouched, in a lacquer scabbard. Some of the tiles are worn smooth. Some are not.

choices.text: Cross the tiles to the sword

ok.log: The tile you guess is the right tile, and the next, and the next. The sword is in your hands: plain, perfect, a thousand years old, its blade of black iron.

fail.deathCause: the turning floor of the general's tomb
fail.log: A tile turns under your foot and you drop into a pit of old spikes and older bones. You climb out with your leg torn open.

choices.text: Step only on the worn tiles

effects.log: The worn ones are the ones the builders walked, carrying the coffin. Step, step, step. You lift the black iron sword and do not take anything else.

choices.text: Bow to the general and leave everything

effects.log: You bow. You leave the sword on the lid. On the way out the stone soldiers seem, in the lamplight, to bow back.

events.text: Outside the tomb, the robber you saved is waiting with two more brothers. They want the tomb's gold. You are in their way.

choices.text: Tell them what is inside

effects.log: Stars, a coffin, a floor that eats people. You describe it all, and the brother you saved starts to shake, and then the others do. They go home.

choices.text: Stand in the gate and refuse

ok.log: Three robbers, one gate. They try. You stand. In the end they go, cursing, and you collapse the gate behind them.

fail.deathCause: tomb robbers at the general's gate
fail.log: Three is too many. You are beaten and left outside the gate while they go in. Only one comes out.

choices.text: Collapse the gate yourself and walk away

effects.log: One kick to the cracked beam. The gate comes down. The robbers swear. Nobody is going into that tomb again in this lifetime.

events.text: In the market, a pill seller with a magnificent beard is selling Heaven-Opening Pills: one breakthrough per pill, guaranteed, cheap. A queue of young martial artists is buying them by the handful. One of them is already looking pale.

choices.text: Buy one to examine, not to take

effects.log: The pill is grey, smells of mushrooms and something sharp. Your nose wrinkles. You keep it wrapped in paper.

choices.text: Ask the pill seller what is in it

effects.log: 'Secret ingredients from the Kunlun peaks,' says the beard, and offers you two for the price of one. The pale young man in the queue throws up behind the stall.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: You walk on. Behind you, the queue grows.

events.text: Three young martial artists who took the Heaven-Opening Pills are lying in a temple courtyard with burning meridians and grey faces. The pill seller has packed his stall. The monks do not know what is in the pills.

choices.text: Push your own qi into them to calm the burning

ok.log: You guide the wild qi down, slowly, into the earth through their feet. One by one, the grey faces turn pink. The monks bow to you.

fail.deathCause: poison qi from a fake pill
fail.log: Their wild qi comes into you instead. Your own meridians burn. You lie beside them in the courtyard for a week.

choices.text: Give the monks the pill you bought, so the healer can test it

effects.log: The healer crushes it and smells it and swears. Dragon's tongue mushroom. There is a remedy. All three live.

choices.text: Run for the town healer

effects.log: The healer comes, takes one look and starts boiling licorice and green beans. Two of the three live. The third will never cultivate again.

events.text: The pill seller with the magnificent beard is in a market two towns over, selling Heaven-Opening Pills again. The beard is dyed black now. The queue is just as long.

choices.text: Expose him in front of the queue

ok.log: You tell the queue about the temple courtyard and the grey faces. The queue becomes a mob. The beard is chased out of town, minus the beard.

fail.log: The beard is very persuasive. The queue laughs at you. You walk away with a pill thrown at your head.

choices.text: Seize him and his stall

ok.log: The beard has bodyguards. Not good ones. You hand him and three sacks of pills to the market headman.

fail.deathCause: the pill seller's bodyguards
fail.log: The bodyguards are better than they looked. You take a knife wound and the beard escapes in the crowd.

choices.text: Buy every pill he has and burn them

effects.log: It costs a fortune. The beard laughs all the way to the next town. But nobody in this one takes a pill tonight.

events.text: On a steep street of a hill town, carters chain their wheels on the way down. A carter with a cart of stone jars tells you the chain on his left wheel is cracked and he cannot afford a new one. 'It will hold,' he says. 'Once more.'

choices.text: Give him the silver for a new chain

effects.log: He stares at the coins, then at you. He goes straight to the smith. You feel very foolish and very good.

choices.text: Tell him it will not hold

effects.log: He shrugs. 'Then I will hold it.' He pats the cart like a horse.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: You walk on up the hill. Behind you, a wheel chain clinks.

events.text: Market day on the steep street. A shout from the top of the hill: a cart of stone jars, its wheel chain snapped, is rolling down through the crowd, gathering speed, and a child is standing in the middle of the street looking at a sugar figure.

choices.text: Throw yourself at the child

ok.log: You scoop the child out of the street as the cart thunders past, a hand's breadth away. Jars burst on the wall at the bottom like fireworks.

fail.deathCause: a runaway cart on a steep street
fail.log: You get the child clear and the cart clips you. You wake in a shop doorway with broken ribs and a crowd around you.

choices.text: Shout and wave the crowd out of the street

effects.log: Your voice carries. The crowd scatters, someone grabs the child. The cart smashes into the wall at the bottom. Nobody is under it.

choices.text: Jam a pole in the spokes as it passes

effects.log: The pole snaps, the cart slews and tips over on its side halfway down the street. Jars everywhere, nobody hurt.

events.text: The carter whose chain snapped has lost his cart and his jars and owes the potter for all of them. He sits on the steps at the bottom of the hill with his head in his hands.

choices.text: Help him pay the potter

effects.log: You pay half. The carter will pay the other half for years. He says you are the only person who did not shout at him.

choices.text: Talk the potter into forgiving the debt

effects.log: The potter is unmoved, then moved, when you mention the child in the street. The debt is halved. The carter cries.

choices.text: Remind him of the chain you paid for

effects.log: He looks at the ground. He drank the silver. He knows. He says he will never drink again. You both know he might.

events.arc: The Face on the Wanted Poster
events.text: On the notice board at the county gate there is a new wanted poster: a bandit called the Grey Fox, three hundred taels, dead or alive. The drawing is crude. It is also, unmistakably, your face.

choices.text: Tear it down

effects.log: It comes off in your hand. A gate guard sees you holding it and looks at the poster, and at you, and starts to frown.

choices.text: Read it carefully for anything that is not you

effects.log: The Grey Fox has a scar through the left eyebrow and is missing a finger on the right hand. You have neither. You remember both.

choices.text: Pull your hat down and leave the county

effects.log: You walk fast and talk to nobody. In the next county there are three more posters. The Grey Fox gets around.

events.arc: The Face on the Wanted Poster
events.text: In an inn yard, three bounty hunters with ropes and clubs surround you. The leader holds up the poster. 'Three hundred taels,' the leader says, 'and we are not fussy about the alive part.'

choices.text: Show them your eyebrow and your hands

effects.log: No scar. Ten fingers. The leader looks at the poster, at you, and swears. One of them wants to take you anyway. The leader smacks him.

choices.text: Fight your way out

ok.log: Three bounty hunters on the ground in an inn yard. Which, you realise as you leave, is exactly what the Grey Fox would have done.

fail.deathCause: bounty hunters who took you for the Grey Fox
fail.log: Three is enough. You wake roped over a horse, on the way to the magistrate, with a split scalp.

choices.text: Talk them into checking with the magistrate first

ok.log: They grumble and march you to the magistrate, who takes one look and laughs. 'The Fox is short.' You are let go.

fail.log: They will not listen. They march you to the county jail and it takes three days for anyone to look at you properly.

choices.text: Hold out your wrists and go quietly

effects.log: They tie you and march you to the magistrate, prodding you all the way. The magistrate takes one look and laughs. 'The Fox is short.' The hunters are fined for your bruises.

events.arc: The Face on the Wanted Poster
events.text: A letter left for you at the inn, in a hand you do not know: 'You have been carrying my name. I have been carrying yours. Shall we meet? The old shrine on Fox Hill. Come alone.'

choices.text: Go alone

ok.log: The Grey Fox is your face with a scar. The Fox wants to talk you into running together. You knock the Fox down instead and drag the Fox to the magistrate.

fail.deathCause: the Grey Fox's ambush on Fox Hill
fail.log: The Fox did not come alone. You come down Fox Hill a day later with two arrow wounds and a lot of questions.

choices.text: Take the letter to the magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate's men wait in the trees around the shrine. The Grey Fox comes, sees too much movement in the trees, and is gone like smoke. But now the magistrate knows the Fox's hill.

choices.text: Burn the letter and leave the province

effects.log: You are tired of your own face. You go west. The posters do not follow you. You hear the Fox was caught a year later, by someone else.

events.arc: The Face on the Wanted Poster
events.text: The Grey Fox is in the magistrate's cage in the town square, waiting for the judgement. Your own face looks out at you through the bars, scarred, with nine fingers, and smiles.

choices.text: Talk to the Fox

effects.log: 'We could have been twins,' the Fox says. 'We could have been anything.' The Fox talks about a poor village and a bad year. You listen. It is your face telling it.

choices.text: Ask the magistrate for mercy for the Fox

effects.log: The magistrate thinks you are mad. The Fox goes to the salt pans instead of the block. When the guards lead the Fox away, the Fox bows to you.

choices.text: Turn your back and walk away

effects.log: Some faces you do not need to see again. The posters come down all over the province. People stop looking at you twice.

events.text: The county magistrate's sixtieth birthday. Two hundred guests, a hundred dishes. In the kitchen yard, sneaking some air, you see a cook you do not recognise pour a vial into the great tureen of shark-fin soup meant for the high table.

choices.text: Follow the cook

effects.log: The cook slips out of the kitchen gate into an alley where a cloaked figure pays in silver. You get a look at the cloaked one: the magistrate's own nephew.

choices.text: Knock the tureen over

effects.log: Two hundred guests hear the crash. The head cook screams at you. The magistrate's guards drag you out of the kitchen. The soup soaks into the floor.

choices.text: Tell the head cook quietly

effects.log: The head cook looks at you, then at the tureen, and pours a ladle of it for the kitchen cat. The cat sniffs it and walks away. The head cook goes pale.

events.text: The high table. The soup is served, or a new soup, or nothing. The nephew is smiling at the magistrate. The cook who poured the vial is standing behind the nephew's chair, holding a tray, very still.

choices.text: Seize the cook before anything else happens

ok.log: The tray goes flying, a hidden knife clatters across the floor. The cook confesses before the guards finish tying the knots, and points at the nephew.

fail.deathCause: a poisoner at the magistrate's feast
fail.log: The cook is quicker than a cook should be. The knife catches you under the arm. The guards finish what you started.

choices.text: Stand and tell the magistrate what you saw

effects.log: Two hundred guests go silent. The magistrate looks at the nephew for a long time. The nephew laughs, and then stops laughing.

choices.text: Whisper to the magistrate's old steward

effects.log: The steward listens, nods, and walks away. Ten minutes later the cook is gone from behind the nephew's chair, and nobody saw it happen.

events.text: A letter in the magistrate's own hand thanks you for the birthday, and nothing else. A purse comes with it. A month later the nephew is posted to a very distant salt office, and the magistrate is seen weeping in the garden.

choices.text: Keep the purse, and the silence

effects.log: It is a heavy purse. You never speak of the feast. The magistrate never forgets you, and in that county your name opens doors.

choices.text: Return the purse and visit the magistrate

effects.log: You sit with the old magistrate in the garden. 'My sister's child,' the magistrate says. 'I taught that one to read.' You do not say anything. You stay until the tea is cold.

choices.text: Use the favour for the town's poor

effects.log: You ask the magistrate to open the granary in the spring. The magistrate does. The town remembers the birthday for a different reason.

events.arc: The Missing Children of Willow Ford
events.text: In Willow Ford, children have been going missing from the riverside at dusk: three this month. The villagers are frantic. An old fisherman says he saw a boat with a red lantern going downstream late, too fast for a fishing boat.

choices.text: Ask the fisherman about the red lantern boat

effects.log: 'Comes up from the city every new moon. Never fishes. Buys nothing. Goes back fast.' The new moon is in nine days.

choices.text: Sit with the mothers and listen

effects.log: You listen to every detail of every child. One of them was wearing a bright red jacket. You fix it in your mind.

choices.text: Search the riverbanks at dusk
