effects.log: You find a child's straw sandal caught in the reeds below the ford, and boat marks in the mud, deep, a heavy boat.

events.arc: The Missing Children of Willow Ford
events.text: The new moon. A boat with a red lantern ties up below Willow Ford in the dark. Two men with sacks climb up the bank toward the houses. On the boat, under a tarpaulin, something is crying softly.

choices.text: Board the boat and fight the boatmen

ok.log: Two boatmen go into the river. Under the tarpaulin, four children, tied, alive. You carry them up the bank one by one to their screaming families.

fail.deathCause: the kidnappers of Willow Ford
fail.log: A third man was hiding on the boat. You are clubbed over the side into the black river and the boat pulls away.

choices.text: Cut the boat's mooring rope and shout the village awake

effects.log: The boat drifts out into the current. The men on the bank run back, find no boat, and run into a village of very angry parents with torches. The boat is found aground at dawn, children inside.

choices.text: Follow the boat downstream along the bank

effects.log: You run all night along the bank. At dawn the boat ties up at a warehouse on the city's edge. You know where they are now.

events.arc: The Missing Children of Willow Ford
events.text: A riverside warehouse at the edge of the city. Barred windows, a guard at the door, a red lantern hanging unlit. From inside, very faintly, a child is singing a Willow Ford nursery song.

choices.text: Break in at night

ok.log: Over the wall, past the guard, through a door. Eleven children in a back room, from four villages. The city magistrate's men find you all at dawn, singing.

fail.deathCause: the kidnappers' warehouse
fail.log: There are more men inside than you thought. You get three children out over the wall before they bring you down.

choices.text: Bring the city magistrate's constables

effects.log: The constables do not believe you, then do, when the singing starts again. They break the door. Eleven children, four villages, all going home.

choices.text: Bribe the guard to look away while you go in

effects.log: The guard takes the silver and looks away. You bring out every child through the back. In the morning the guard is gone, and so is the gang.

events.arc: The Missing Children of Willow Ford
events.text: Willow Ford has built a watchtower by the river with a bell in it. The children who came home take turns ringing it at dusk. One of them, in a faded red jacket, sees you on the road and runs down the bank to meet you.

choices.text: Let the child show you the bell

effects.log: The child rings it, very hard, and explains the rules of the watchtower at great length. It is the best thing you have heard all year.

choices.text: Sit with the families for the evening meal

effects.log: Every house wants you. You eat five dinners. The fisherman who saw the red lantern sits beside you at every one.

choices.text: Ask about the children who did not come home

effects.log: Two. Taken before the boat was found. The village has put up two little shrines by the watchtower. You light incense at both.

events.text: The silver mine in the hills pays three times a farmhand's wage. The miners say the old gallery is safe if you listen to the timbers. 'They talk before they break,' says a miner with grey dust in every wrinkle. 'Creak is fine. Crack is run.'

choices.text: Take the work for a season

effects.log: Dark, wet, hot. The pay is good. You learn to listen to the timbers, and to hate the dark.

choices.text: Bring the miners food and ask about the galleries

effects.log: The miners know every gallery by name: Long Gallery, Widow's Gallery, Thirsty Gallery. They do not go into Widow's Gallery. You do not ask why.

choices.text: Refuse: the dark is not for you

effects.log: The miners laugh. You go back to farm work. The farmhand's wage seems very fair in the sunlight.

events.text: Deep in the Long Gallery. A sound from the timbers above you, not a creak. A crack, like a dry branch. Dust sifts down in the lamplight. Ahead of you, three miners have not heard it over their picks.

choices.text: Shout CRACK and run back toward the shaft

effects.log: Your shout and the miners' heads coming up and all four of you running, and the gallery roof coming down behind you like a closing door.

choices.text: Run forward and drag the miners back

ok.log: You grab two collars and the third miner runs with you. The roof comes down where they were kneeling. In the shaft, four of you sit coughing and laughing.

fail.deathCause: a cave-in in the silver mine
fail.log: The roof comes down on you all. You are dug out after a day and a night, alive in an air pocket with the miners, very thirsty.

choices.text: Run for the shaft and ring the alarm

effects.log: You ring the mine bell. Miners come running from everywhere. The roof comes down. Two of the three get out. The third is dug out the next day, alive.

events.text: The mine owner wants to reopen the Long Gallery at once, cheaply, without new timbers. The miners are angry and afraid. They look at you: the one who heard the crack.

choices.text: Speak for the miners to the owner

effects.log: The owner is a soft-handed man who has never been underground. You take him down, and let him hear the timbers talk. He orders new timbers the next day.

choices.text: Lead the miners in refusing to go down

effects.log: No miner goes down for nine days. On the tenth, the owner gives in. New timbers, a second shaft for air. The miners carve your name in the shaft wall.

choices.text: Leave the mine for good

effects.log: You walk out into the sunlight and keep walking. Some work is not worth any wage. The miner with grey wrinkles waves from the shaft mouth.

events.arc: The Pirate Flag in the Fog
events.text: On the coastal road, every fishing village has a watchman on the headland. 'Pirates from the islands,' a fisherwoman says, gutting fish. 'Black sails. They come in fog. Last month they took the whole village of Three Rocks, boats and people.'

choices.text: Ask what happened to the people

effects.log: 'Sold,' she says, and does not look up. 'Or rowing.' Her knife does not stop. You remember the name Three Rocks.

choices.text: Offer to stand watch on the headland

effects.log: Cold nights, a horn, and a lot of staring at the sea. The fisherwoman brings you fish soup. It is very good fish soup.

choices.text: Walk on before the fog season

effects.log: You take the inland road. In the next town there is news: another village burned on the coast.

events.arc: The Pirate Flag in the Fog
events.text: Fog on the sea at dawn. From the headland you hear oars, many oars, and see the black mast of a ship sliding through the grey toward the village beach. The village is asleep.

choices.text: Blow the horn and keep blowing it

effects.log: The horn goes out over the village like a scream. People pour out of the houses and up the hill with what they can carry. The pirates find an empty beach.

choices.text: Run down to the beach and meet them at the waterline

ok.log: You meet the first boat as it grounds, and the second. They did not expect a fight. They row back into the fog with their wounded.

fail.deathCause: island pirates on the coastal beach
fail.log: There are too many boats. You are knocked down in the surf and kicked and left for dead on the sand.

choices.text: Run through the village banging on doors

effects.log: House to house, shouting. Half the village gets up the hill. The pirates take the boats and the nets, and one old man who would not leave.

events.arc: The Pirate Flag in the Fog
events.text: The pirates' black-sailed ship is anchored in a cove on one of the islands. A fisherman says the people of Three Rocks are kept there, chained in the hold, waiting for a buyer from the south.

choices.text: Swim out at night and free them

ok.log: A long cold swim, a slippery anchor chain, a hold full of frightened people and a lot of quiet work with a file. By dawn there are forty people on the beach and a ship with no rowers.

fail.deathCause: the pirate ship in the island cove
fail.log: A sentry sees you on the chain. You fall into the sea with an arrow in your back and drift ashore at dawn, barely alive.

choices.text: Bring the coast guard captain to the cove

effects.log: The captain does not want to go. You shame the captain into it. Three war junks round the island at dawn. The people of Three Rocks come home.

choices.text: Tell the families of Three Rocks where their people are

effects.log: They buy a boat together, and sail at night, and come back with half of them. Half is not all. Half is a great many.

events.arc: The Pirate Flag in the Fog
events.text: Three Rocks is a village again: new houses, new boats, a new watchman on the headland. The fisherwoman from the coastal road has moved here and is gutting fish on the beach, and laughs to see you.

choices.text: Eat fish soup with her on the beach

effects.log: The best fish soup on the coast, she says, and she is right. The people of Three Rocks come down to the beach one by one to sit with you.

choices.text: Help them build a signal fire on the headland

effects.log: A beacon, ready to light, that the next village can see. And the next. Soon a chain of fires runs the whole coast.

choices.text: Walk on down the coast

effects.log: You leave before the feast. The watchman on the headland blows the horn once as you go, not for pirates. For you.

events.text: A village in the valley has hung white cloths on its gate: fever. The road runs straight through it. A fearful official at the barricade says nobody goes in or out, by order. Behind the barricade a child is calling for water.

choices.text: Take the long road round

effects.log: Two days round the valley. You hear the child calling for an hour, fading.

choices.text: Leave your waterskin at the barricade

effects.log: The official will not take it across. A woman from inside the village does. She bows to you over the barricade, a cloth over her mouth.

choices.text: Ask the official what the fever is

effects.log: Red spots, burning, a cough. The official is terrified and knows nothing else. The village healer, the official says, died in the first week.

events.text: The fever village again. The barricade guards have fled. Inside, half the houses are shut and silent, and in the temple the sick lie in rows with nobody to tend them. Anyone who goes in may take the fever out.

choices.text: Go in and nurse the sick

ok.log: Water, cool cloths, rice broth. Two weeks with a cloth over your face. You do not catch it. Many who would have died do not.

fail.deathCause: the valley fever
fail.log: You catch it. For a week you lie in the rows with them, burning. You wake one morning thin as a reed, alive.

choices.text: Bring a healer from the town

effects.log: The town healer refuses, then is shamed into coming, then works harder than anyone. You carry water. The fever breaks in a month.

choices.text: Leave food and medicine at the gate every day

effects.log: Every morning, a sack at the gate. Someone inside takes it. The village lives on it for a month.

events.text: The fever has passed. The village is burning its bedding in a great fire on the threshing floor. The woman who took your waterskin at the barricade is in charge now; the headman died in the second week.

choices.text: Help with the burning and the burials

effects.log: Two weeks of hard, sad work. When you leave, the village gives you the only thing it has: a jar of plum preserves from the headman's cellar.

choices.text: Ask what the village needs

effects.log: A healer, seed rice, a new headman. You can find the first two. The woman with the cloth, they decide, is the third.

choices.text: Write down what the fever did, for the county

effects.log: Red spots, the cough, how long, how many. The county healer reads it and sends copies to every village in the province.

events.text: Years later, a fever with red spots appears in a town on the river. The county healer, now old, remembers your notes. This time the town is ready: boiled water, a sick house, cloths. Few die.

choices.text: Go and help, now that you know how

effects.log: You have done this before. You do it again, faster. The town healers watch you and copy you. The fever is gone in three weeks.

choices.text: Send silver and seed rice instead

effects.log: A cart of seed rice and a purse. The town plants in the spring as if nothing had happened.

choices.text: Visit the fever village and see how it is

effects.log: Children everywhere, a new temple roof, a woman who was once in charge now very old, sitting in the sun. She knows you at once.

events.text: On the stone stairs of a holy mountain, pilgrims are hurrying down. An old porter with a load of firewood looks at the clouds building over the summit. 'Afternoon thunder,' he says. 'On the top it hunts anyone standing. Lie down in a hollow, never under the lone pine.'

choices.text: Turn back with the pilgrims

effects.log: You go down. Behind you, at the top, the sky goes purple. You hear the thunder hit the summit three times and feel it in your knees.

choices.text: Ask why the lone pine

effects.log: 'Because it is the tallest thing. Heaven likes the tallest thing.' He laughs. 'Do not be the tallest thing.'

choices.text: Keep climbing; the summit temple is close

effects.log: The porter shakes his head and goes down. You climb on.

events.text: The storm comes on the summit faster than anything you have ever seen. Your hair stands up on end. The air buzzes. The stone stairs hum under your feet. The only shelter in sight is a lone pine on the ridge.

choices.text: Lie flat in a hollow in the rocks

effects.log: You lie in a hollow with your hands over your head. The lightning hits the summit again and again. It hits the lone pine and splits it to the root.

choices.text: Run for the summit temple

ok.log: You reach the temple door as the sky splits open behind you. The monks pull you in. Outside, the world is white and loud.

fail.deathCause: lightning on the holy peak
fail.log: The lightning strikes the stairs ahead of you. The world goes white. You wake with your clothes smoking and a tree-shaped mark on your arm.

choices.text: Crouch low on the stairs, feet together

effects.log: The old porter said something about that. You crouch, feet together, head down, and the storm walks around you like a giant looking for something taller.

choices.text: Shelter under the lone pine

effects.log: The pine is dry under its branches. You hear a buzzing in the bark. You run out of it just before it is split in two.

events.text: In the summit temple after the storm, a monk with a burned hand is laughing. He was struck too, years ago, and lived. 'Heaven touched you,' he says. 'It does not do that for nothing. Sit with me and see what it left.'

choices.text: Sit with the monk and meditate

effects.log: In the silence after the storm, something in your meridians has shifted, as if a door had been knocked open. You sit until dawn, feeling it.

choices.text: Ask the monk what it left him

effects.log: 'Fear,' he says, 'for a year. Then none. Fear of nothing, ever again.' He laughs. 'It is a good trade.'

choices.text: Go down the mountain and do not look back

effects.log: You go down in the clear morning. The pilgrims coming up stare at your singed hair. You do not explain.

events.text: Small wrong things. A beggar you have never seen before watches your door for three days. The innkeeper says someone asked which room you sleep in. A dog that always barks at you is found dead in the alley, quietly.

choices.text: Change rooms every night

effects.log: A different room, a different inn. It is tiring and expensive and makes you feel foolish. Then you find a hole drilled in the wall of the room you did not sleep in.

choices.text: Follow the beggar

effects.log: The beggar leads you to a teahouse where a man in grey pays him. The man in grey does not look back. You know the face now.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: Small wrong things happen to everyone. You sleep in the same room. On the fourth night you wake with a start at a sound at the window, and nothing is there.

events.text: A friend of a friend, a broker in the dark trade, sends you a message: there is a contract on your name with the Silent Needle House. Three hundred taels. Someone hates you very much. The Needle never misses, the broker adds.

choices.text: Ask the broker who paid

effects.log: The broker will not say. The broker will say it was paid in gold from the south, and that the Needle sends one assassin at a time, and that there are three left in the House.

choices.text: Pay the broker to try and buy the contract back

effects.log: The broker tries. The House refuses. 'A contract is a contract.' But the broker gives you a description of the first assassin: a woman who sells flowers.

choices.text: Leave the province at once

effects.log: You leave by night. In the next province, three days later, a flower seller smiles at you in the market. You walk the other way very fast.

events.text: In a crowded market, a flower seller steps into your path with a basket of white lilies, smiling. Her left hand is under the flowers. The crowd is thick on both sides. There is nowhere to step.

choices.text: Catch her wrist before it comes out

ok.log: Her hand comes out with a needle as long as your finger, and stops in your grip. Her smile does not change. Then she twists free and is gone into the crowd, without her basket.

fail.deathCause: the Silent Needle House
fail.log: The needle goes into your side, under the ribs. Your legs fold. A healer in the crowd saves you, by luck, with a pill that costs more than your horse.

choices.text: Knock the basket out of her hands first

effects.log: Lilies everywhere. The needle in her hand is suddenly in plain view of fifty people. She smiles at you, and turns, and walks away, very fast.

choices.text: Step back into the noodle stall behind you

effects.log: You crash into the noodle stall. Boiling water, shouting, a scalded cook. When you look up, the flower seller is gone, and a lily is stuck in your sleeve with a needle through its stem.

events.text: A second assassin, a third: a monk who almost reaches you on a bridge, a child sent with a poisoned cake that you do not eat. The Silent Needle House has one assassin left, the broker says. The master of the House himself.

choices.text: Go to the Needle House and end it

roll.foeName: the master of the Needle House

ok.log: A shabby house behind a dye works. An old man in grey, very still. The fight lasts a breath. When it is over, the contract is burned in front of you.

fail.deathCause: the master of the Silent Needle House
fail.log: He is faster than anything you have ever faced. You get away with a needle in your shoulder and the contract still alive.

choices.text: Find out who paid, and why

effects.log: Gold from the south. A name. Someone you defeated years ago, and humiliated, and forgot. You had forgotten. They had not.

choices.text: Pay the House double to break the contract

effects.log: The broker carries your silver to the House. The master considers it for a long time. 'Double is a new contract,' the master says. 'Ours.' It is broken.

events.text: The contract is over, one way or another. One evening a letter is delivered by a child who runs away at once. It is from the person in the south who paid the Silent Needle House. It says only: 'Why are you still alive?'

choices.text: Write back and apologise for the old humiliation

effects.log: You do not know if it will matter. A year later a second letter comes: 'I hated you for twenty years. Now I do not know what to do.' You write again.

choices.text: Write back: because I listened to small wrong things

effects.log: No reply comes. You keep changing rooms, a little, for the rest of your life, out of habit.

choices.text: Burn the letter unanswered

effects.log: You burn it. Some people have to be left alone with their questions.

events.arc: The Son of the Man You Beat
events.text: A young martial artist, {npc}, stands in the road ahead of you with a sword {he} cannot quite handle yet. 'Years ago you broke my father in a duel,' {npc} says. 'Father never fought again. The wine did the rest. I am going to kill you.'

choices.text: Fight, and spare {him}

ok.log: It is over quickly. You take {his} sword and give it back. 'Come back when you can use it.' {npc} goes away white with fury and shame.

fail.log: {npc} is better than {he} looks. You win, with a cut across your arm and a lot to think about.

choices.text: Refuse to fight, and walk past

effects.log: {npc} shouts at your back for half a li. You do not turn round. That night you dream of an old duel you had nearly forgotten.

choices.text: Ask {npc} about the father

effects.log: {npc} did not expect that. The father taught the village children for free, after. And drank. And talked about you every night. {npc} walks away crying with anger.

events.arc: The Son of the Man You Beat
events.text: Your tea at the inn tastes of almonds. You spit it out. At the next table {npc} is watching you over a cup, white-faced, {his} hands shaking. A sword is one thing. Poison is another.

choices.text: Sit down at {npc}'s table

mem.note: sat at my table after the poison

effects.log: You sit. {npc} cannot look at you. 'I could not make my hand stop shaking,' {npc} says. 'With the sword.' You order two clean cups.

choices.text: Drag {npc} to the magistrate

ok.log: {npc} does not resist. The magistrate jails {him} for a year. When {he} comes out, you are waiting at the gate. {npc} looks at you as if you were a ghost.

fail.log: {npc} draws a knife at the last moment and you take it in the hand. {npc} runs.

choices.text: Leave a coin for the tea and go

effects.log: You leave without a word. {npc} follows you to the town gate and then stops, as if a rope had pulled tight.

events.arc: The Son of the Man You Beat
events.text: A storm night on a mountain road. You round a bend and find {npc} pinned under a fallen cart, the river rising toward {him} in the dark. {npc} sees who it is and laughs, horribly. 'Go on. Leave me.'

choices.text: Lift the cart off {him}

mem.note: lifted the cart off me in the storm

ok.log: You heave the cart up and {npc} drags out from under it. You carry {him} to the next village on your back, neither of you speaking.

mem.note: tried to save me in the storm

fail.log: The cart slips and crushes your leg too. You both lie in the mud, laughing, until a woodcutter comes and gets you both out.

choices.text: Dig the mud out from under {npc} with your hands

mem.note: dug me out from under the cart

effects.log: Slow work, in the rain, with the river at your knees. {npc} slides out from under the cart at last. 'Why?' {npc} asks. You do not have an answer.

choices.text: Run for help in the village

effects.log: You run. The villagers come with ropes and lift the cart. {npc} is pulled out half drowned, alive. You are not there when {he} wakes.

events.arc: The Son of the Man You Beat
events.text: {npc} comes to find you, older, with a plain sword and a plain face. {He} kneels in the road where {he} first stood to challenge you. 'I want to learn,' {npc} says. 'From the one who broke my father. So that I can teach better than my father did.'

choices.text: Teach {npc}

effects.log: You teach {npc} the sword for a year. {npc} is good, and patient, and never mentions the father. On the last day {npc} bows to you. 'Father would have liked you,' {npc} says.

choices.text: Take {npc} to the father's grave first

effects.log: You kneel at the grave together. You say what you should have said years ago. {npc} listens. Then you both get up, and it is over.

choices.text: Refuse, but give {npc} your own first manual

effects.log: 'I am the wrong teacher.' You give {npc} the manual you learned from as a child. {npc} takes it like something alive.

events.text: A smiling stranger in a teahouse sells you, for very little, a copied manual of the Cloud-Piercing Breath, a method you have long wanted. The copy is beautiful. On page eleven, one character in the meridian chart has been scraped and redrawn.

choices.text: Study the redrawn character carefully

effects.log: The original line runs through the Sea of Qi. The new one runs backward, into the heart. A small change. A practitioner would not notice until it was too late.

choices.text: Practise from it at once

effects.log: The first nights are wonderful: warmth, speed, a rush like wine. On the fifth night your heart skips three beats in a row and does not want to start again.

choices.text: Put it away until you can check it

effects.log: You lock it in your pack. Something about the stranger's smile was too wide.

events.text: Night. You are sitting in meditation when the qi you have been circulating turns, all at once, like a horse that has seen a snake, and runs backward toward your heart. Your chest is on fire. This is how deviations kill.

choices.text: Force it back along the true path

ok.log: You drag the qi round, line by line, against the pull. Toward dawn it settles back into the Sea of Qi, sullen and tamed. You are soaked through.

fail.deathCause: qi deviation from a tampered manual
fail.log: It breaks loose. Something tears inside your chest. You wake on the floor at noon with a taste of iron in your mouth and a heartbeat like a cracked bell.

choices.text: Stop circulating at once, and let the qi scatter

effects.log: You let it go. It scatters, painfully, out of every meridian at once. Months of gathered qi are gone. You are alive.

choices.text: You saw the redrawn line: follow the old one instead

effects.log: You know the trap. You walk your qi along the true line, through the Sea of Qi, around the false turning. The deviation never takes hold.

events.text: In another teahouse, another town, the smiling stranger is selling another beautiful copy to an eager young disciple. The stranger sees you and the smile stays exactly where it is.

choices.text: Seize the stranger

ok.log: The stranger fights like a cornered cat and loses. In the bag: forty manuals, all beautifully copied, all with one line changed. A rival sect's work.

fail.deathCause: the false manual seller
fail.log: The stranger throws powder in your eyes and is gone. You spend an hour half blind, warning the young disciple not to read page eleven.

choices.text: Take the disciple aside and show page eleven

effects.log: The disciple looks at the redrawn line, goes pale, and tears the manual in two. The stranger is gone when you look back.

choices.text: Buy every copy the stranger has, and burn them

effects.log: The stranger sells cheerfully, at a higher price. You burn forty manuals behind the inn. It is a very expensive fire.

events.text: At a pawnshop in a river town, a sword hangs on the wall in a black lacquer scabbard. It is cheap, very cheap. The pawnbroker will not touch it and says three owners have pawned it, and none came back for it. When you stand near it, you hear, very faintly, something like breathing.

choices.text: Buy it

effects.log: The pawnbroker takes the silver with enormous relief and wraps the sword in three layers of cloth without touching it. That night, by your bed, it breathes.

choices.text: Ask about the three owners

effects.log: One fought a duel and won and fought another and won, and another, until he lost. One killed a friend in an argument. One, the pawnbroker says, simply walked into the river.

choices.text: Leave it on the wall

effects.log: You walk out. The breathing follows you to the door and stops, as if disappointed.

events.text: The sword has been talking. Not in words: in wanting. In a crowded street a drunk shoves you, and your hand is on the hilt before you think, and the sword is purring, and the drunk is very close.

choices.text: Take your hand off the hilt

ok.log: Finger by finger. The sword screams in your head like a kettle. The drunk staggers away, never knowing how close it was. You are shaking.

fail.deathCause: the whispering sword
fail.log: It comes out of the scabbard by itself, or you draw it, you are never sure which. You turn it at the last moment into your own leg.

choices.text: Let the drunk go and walk away fast

effects.log: You walk with your hands in your sleeves, all the way to the river, and stand there until the purring stops.

choices.text: Hand the sword, scabbard and all, to a temple

effects.log: The abbot takes it with tongs, wraps it in a sutra and puts it under the great bell. The breathing stops. The abbot is not surprised. 'We have a few of these.'

events.text: The sword's whispering has a shape now: a name, a mountain, a grave. A swordsman who died in a duel he should have won, a hundred years ago, and has been looking for an arm ever since. It wants to go home.

choices.text: Carry it to the swordsman's grave

ok.log: Up the mountain for three days, with the sword fighting you every step. At the grave it goes quiet. You bury it there, and something old and tired lets go of you.

fail.deathCause: the whispering sword
fail.log: On the narrow path above the gorge the sword twists in your hands toward the edge. You hold on and fall, together, and only a pine stops you.

choices.text: Let a monk carry it, and walk beside them

effects.log: Two of you, one sword, a monk chanting the whole way. At the grave the sword goes into the earth without a sound.

choices.text: Talk to it as a swordsman to a swordsman

effects.log: You tell it about your own duels, the ones you won and the ones you lost and lived. It listens. It goes quiet, for a long time.

events.text: Years later, at the swordsman's grave on the mountain, an old pine has grown over the place where you buried the sword. When the wind blows through it there is a sound like breathing, peaceful now, like someone asleep.

choices.text: Sit by the pine and practise

effects.log: Your sword in the clearing, alone. The pine breathes. Every cut feels watched by someone who knows, and approves.

choices.text: Leave a cup of wine at the grave

effects.log: For a swordsman who should have won. The wind takes the smell of the wine up into the pine. You walk down feeling lighter.

choices.text: Carve a warning on the pawnshop wall in town

effects.log: THREE OWNERS, the carving says, and a fourth who brought it home. The pawnbroker reads it aloud to every customer.

events.text: On a mountain road at dusk, a Taoist corpse-driver passes with a little bell, leading a line of the dead home to their villages, tall paper charms on their foreheads, hopping. 'Do not walk this road at night,' the driver says. 'If a charm comes loose, they do not know you from a stranger.'

choices.text: Stop at the next village for the night

effects.log: The village keeps its doors shut and its lamps lit. At midnight you hear the bell go past outside, and something hopping, and then nothing.

choices.text: Ask what to do if a charm comes loose

effects.log: 'Hold your breath. They find the living by breath. And never run: they are faster than you think.' The driver rings the bell and moves on.

choices.text: Offer to walk with the driver

effects.log: The driver looks at you a long time. 'A living one at the back is a good thing. They behave when they are watched.' You walk all night behind the dead.

events.text: Midnight on the mountain road. Ahead, a little bell has stopped ringing. In the road, a yellow charm lies in the dust. Something tall and stiff is standing very still beside it, and its head is turning slowly toward the sound of your breathing.

choices.text: Hold your breath and stand still

effects.log: You hold your breath until your vision goes black at the edges. The tall thing hops past you, a hand's breadth away, and on down the road, and is gone.

choices.text: Pick up the charm and slap it back on its forehead

ok.log: You dart in and slap it on. The tall thing goes rigid and still. Down the road, the corpse-driver comes running, ringing the bell like mad.

fail.deathCause: a corpse loose on the mountain road
fail.log: It is faster than you think. Its stiff arms close around you like a vice. You get the charm back on with your last breath, and lie there crushed.

choices.text: Back away into the trees, slowly

effects.log: You back away into the trees and stand with your back to a cedar until dawn. The road is empty in the morning, and the charm is gone.

events.text: The corpse-driver finds you in the village the next day, ringing the little bell softly, and bows. 'The one that came loose was going home to a mother who has waited ten years. Will you help me take it the last part of the way?'

choices.text: Walk the last li with the driver

effects.log: At the village gate an old woman comes out and touches the dead face with both hands. The driver rings the bell once. You do not speak all the way back.

choices.text: Pay for the burial

effects.log: The family is very poor. You pay for a proper grave and a stone. The old woman holds your hands for a long time and says nothing at all.

choices.text: Ask the driver to teach you the bell

effects.log: Three rings for walk, one for stop. The driver lets you lead the line for a li. The dead follow you, hopping, obedient. It is the strangest hour of your life.

events.text: A beautiful, polite master of the Hundred Poisons Valley stops you at a crossroads, smiles, and touches your wrist as if taking your pulse. 'You have three days,' the master says. 'The Seven-Step Lotus. Bring me the Jade Ledger your host keeps, and I bring you the antidote.' A cold thread is already climbing your arm.

choices.text: Ask what happens on the third day

effects.log: 'Your heart stops on the third sunset. Very peaceful.' The master smiles. 'Do not run too much. It makes it faster.'

choices.text: Go straight to the best healer in town

effects.log: The healer feels your pulse and goes grey. 'Seven-Step Lotus. I can slow it. I cannot stop it. Only the one who made it can.' You have more time now.

choices.text: Seize the master now

effects.log: The master is not there any more. Only a smell of lotus at the crossroads, and laughter, far off, like a bell.

events.text: The second day. The cold thread has reached your shoulder. Your host, the old merchant who keeps the Jade Ledger, is kind and trusting and has no idea. The ledger is on the desk. In it, every secret debt of every sect in the province.

choices.text: Tell your host everything

effects.log: The old merchant listens, very still. Then goes to a cupboard and comes back with a small jade bottle. 'My wife was of the Hundred Poisons Valley,' the merchant says. 'She left me this, for this.'

choices.text: Steal the ledger and go to the crossroads

ok.log: You take it at night. The master meets you at the crossroads and gives you the antidote. It works. You will never forgive yourself.

fail.deathCause: the Seven-Step Lotus poison
fail.log: The master takes the ledger, laughs, and gives you a bottle of water. You are dying on the crossroads before you understand.

choices.text: Burn out the poison with your own qi

ok.log: All night, every thread of qi you have, pushed down your arm and out through your fingertips, dripping black. At dawn the cold is gone.

fail.deathCause: the Seven-Step Lotus poison
fail.log: The poison follows your qi back up into your heart. You lie on the floor until the healer finds you.

events.text: The third sunset. You are alive. At the crossroads, the master of the Hundred Poisons Valley is waiting, and sees you standing, and stops smiling for the first time.

choices.text: Fight the poison master

ok.log: The fight is all smoke and needles and you are faster. When it ends, the master is on the ground, laughing again. 'Good. Very good.' And gives you a token of the Valley.

fail.deathCause: the master of the Hundred Poisons Valley
fail.log: The master's needles find you three times. Different poisons. You crawl back to town to the healer, three days of fever.

choices.text: Bow, and walk away

effects.log: The master stares at you, then laughs and bows back. 'Nobody has ever just bowed.' You walk away with your back to the master, which is the bravest thing you have ever done.

choices.text: Ask the master why

effects.log: 'Because the ledger would make me queen of the province. Because you were there.' The master shrugs. 'Nothing personal. Now it is.' And is gone in lotus smoke.

events.text: A box arrives with no name on it: a jade bottle of the Seven-Step Lotus antidote, a cutting of a lotus plant, and a note. 'For the next one I poison. I will send them to you. You seem to have the knack.'

choices.text: Keep the antidote safe

effects.log: It is a good thing to have. Two years later a stranger with a cold thread in the arm comes to your door. You save the stranger.

choices.text: Plant the lotus and study it

effects.log: It is a beautiful plant and deadly in every part. You learn more about poison from it than from any manual.

choices.text: Send the token back to the Valley with a refusal

effects.log: The token comes back a month later with a single lotus petal. You do not know what it means. You decide it means respect.

events.text: In the river towns, the Flying Dagger Gang robs travellers from rooftops: a dagger in the shoulder from nowhere, a purse gone. A dumpling seller points at the rooftops with a ladle. 'They like the quiet streets at dusk. They like people who look rich.'

choices.text: Dress plainly and keep to busy streets

effects.log: You wear your oldest clothes. Nobody looks at you twice. The rooftops stay quiet.

choices.text: Watch the rooftops at dusk

effects.log: Three shapes on the tiles, quick as cats, moving toward the quiet streets. One of them is very small, a child.

choices.text: Walk the quiet streets at dusk with a fat purse

effects.log: Bait. You walk slowly, jingling. Something glints on the rooftop. You duck into a doorway just as a dagger thuds into the post.

events.text: A quiet street at dusk. A whistle from the rooftops. Three daggers come down out of the dusk at you, one after another, fast as wasps.

choices.text: Catch them out of the air

ok.log: One, two, three. You catch the last one by the blade, stop it a finger from your eye, and throw it back up. A yelp from the roof. The gang scatters.

fail.deathCause: the Flying Dagger Gang
fail.log: Two, not three. The third goes into your side. You stagger into a shop as the gang drops down for your purse.

choices.text: Throw yourself flat behind a water barrel

effects.log: Three thuds in the barrel. Water everywhere. You lie in the wet until the whistle sounds again, further away.

choices.text: Shout up at the smallest one by name of the street

effects.log: 'Little one! Dumpling Street! Granny is looking for you!' It is a guess. The small shape on the roof freezes, and the others hesitate, and you run.

events.text: You find their nest: an attic above a burned-out dye works, with straw beds and a hoard of purses. The gang is three orphans and one grown man who taught them to throw. The man is asleep. The children are not.

choices.text: Fight the man

ok.log: He wakes with a dagger in each hand and you take them away from him. The children watch in silence. The magistrate gets the man. You get the children.

fail.deathCause: the master of the Flying Dagger Gang
fail.log: He is the best thrower you have ever seen. You get out of the attic with two daggers in your arm.

choices.text: Talk to the children while he sleeps

effects.log: They are hungry, frightened and very good at throwing. You offer them a temple, rice and a teacher who does not send them onto roofs. Two of three come.

choices.text: Fetch the constables

effects.log: The constables come in force. The man goes to jail and the children run off over the roofs. You see one of them, months later, begging.

events.text: A valley where two armies fought three hundred years ago. Nothing grows in a perfect ring at its centre. Herders say anyone who steps into the ring walks in circles until they die, and the old general's banners still fly there at night.

choices.text: Look at the ring from the hillside

effects.log: From above, you can see it: stones in the grass, half-buried, in a pattern. A formation, old and still working, faint as breath.

choices.text: Throw a stone into the ring

effects.log: The stone lands, rolls, and keeps rolling, round and round in a slow circle, until it stops exactly where it started.

choices.text: Keep well away

effects.log: You walk round the valley. That night by your fire you hear, faint and far, a war drum.

events.text: A shepherd boy has followed a lamb into the ring. He is walking in a slow circle, his face blank, the lamb at his heels. He has been walking since dawn. His feet are bleeding.

choices.text: Walk in and pull him out

ok.log: You walk in counting your steps backwards, the way formations are broken. The ring pulls at you like a current. You come out with the boy and the lamb.

fail.deathCause: the old battlefield formation
fail.log: The ring takes you too. You walk with him in circles until dark, when the boy's father throws a rope and hauls you both out.

choices.text: Throw him a rope from outside the ring

effects.log: The rope lands across his path. He walks into it. You haul. He comes out of the ring like a fish out of a pool, blinking, with the lamb in his arms.

choices.text: Move one of the buried stones

effects.log: From the edge you dig out a stone that breaks the pattern. The ring sighs. The boy stops walking and sits down and cries.

events.text: You come back with spades and the herders, to dig out the old general's stones. Under the first one is a bronze tablet with an oath on it: the general swore to hold this valley until the war was won. The war ended three hundred years ago.

choices.text: Read the oath aloud, and announce the war is over

effects.log: In the silence after, the wind changes. That night, no drum. The herders say the general heard.

choices.text: Bury the tablet with honour on the hillside

effects.log: A small grave, a stick of incense. The ring grows grass by spring.

choices.text: Keep the tablet as a study of old formations

effects.log: The old formation is clever, cleverer than any you have seen. You learn from it for years.

events.arc: The Beast Tide from Mist Mountain
events.text: Something is wrong on Mist Mountain. Deer run through the villages in daylight. Boars come down into the fields and do not care about dogs. An old hunter says it has happened twice in his lifetime: something big has woken in the mountain, and everything else is running from it.

choices.text: Help the villages build palisades

effects.log: Sharpened logs round the three nearest villages. Hard work, fast work. The headmen think you are mad. Then a herd of spirit-touched boars hits the first palisade and breaks against it.

choices.text: Go up to see what woke

effects.log: You climb to the tree line. Everything you meet is running downhill. Above, in the mist, something breathes like a forge.

choices.text: Warn the county and leave

effects.log: The county sends a clerk to write things down. You leave. A month later Mist Mountain is a name in every teahouse.

events.arc: The Beast Tide from Mist Mountain
events.text: The beast tide comes down at dawn: spirit wolves, red-eyed boars, a bear as big as a hut, all running from the mountain in a wave of fur and noise, straight at the village where you are sleeping.

choices.text: Hold the gate

ok.log: You stand in the gate and the tide breaks round you like a river round a stone. When it passes, the village stands. You can barely lift your arms.

fail.deathCause: the beast tide from Mist Mountain
fail.log: The great bear goes through the gate and through you. You wake in the wreck of a house, and the village is half gone.

choices.text: Get the villagers onto the temple roof

effects.log: Ladders, ropes, children handed up. The tide pours through the lanes beneath you. Nobody on the roof is lost.

choices.text: Man the palisade you built

effects.log: The palisade holds, mostly. Where it breaks, you are there with a spear. By noon the tide has gone round the village and down the valley.

events.arc: The Beast Tide from Mist Mountain
events.text: The thing that woke in Mist Mountain has come down after the tide, slow, enormous, wreathed in mist: a spirit boar as big as a temple, its tusks like curved pillars, hungry after a hundred years of sleep.

choices.text: Fight it on the mountain road

ok.log: The longest fight of your life, all afternoon on the road above the valley. At dusk it goes down, and the mountain is quiet. One of its great tusks lies broken in the road, glowing faintly.

fail.deathCause: the great spirit boar of Mist Mountain
fail.log: It is a hundred years of strength. You are thrown off the road into the gorge, and lie there for a day before the hunters find you.

choices.text: Lead it away from the villages with fire

effects.log: Torches, smoke, a long run up the ridge with it behind you. It follows the fire back up into the mist, and stops, and lies down to sleep again.

choices.text: Leave it offerings and let it pass

effects.log: The hunters' old way: a pile of grain and salt at the foot of the mountain. It eats, and goes back up. Nobody knows if it will come again.

events.arc: The Beast Tide from Mist Mountain
events.text: The valleys under Mist Mountain are rebuilding. The old hunter has carved a stone at the foot of the road: the year of the beast tide, and the year before, and the one before that. Three dates, eighty years apart.

choices.text: Add your own record to the stone

effects.log: What woke, how it came, what stopped it. In eighty years someone will read it.

choices.text: Help the villages move their fields further from the mountain

effects.log: It is a hard thing to ask of farmers. They do it. The next tide, eighty years later, finds empty fields.

choices.text: Drink with the old hunter

effects.log: He tells you about the last tide, when he was a boy. You tell him about this one. Neither of you says the word afraid, and both of you were.

events.arc: The Cave of the Red Centipede
events.text: An alchemist pays well for Red Dragon Moss, which grows only in one cave in the southern hills. 'There is a guardian,' the alchemist admits. 'A centipede. A big one. It sleeps in the day, mostly. Do not wake it. And do not let it bite you.'

choices.text: Ask how big

effects.log: The alchemist holds out both arms. Then, after a moment, takes a step back and holds them out again.

choices.text: Buy the alchemist's realgar powder

effects.log: Yellow powder that stinks of rotten eggs. 'Centipedes hate it. Scatter it, and they keep away. Mostly.'

choices.text: Refuse the job

effects.log: The alchemist sighs and hires someone else. You hear in the market that the someone else came back without the moss, and without one boot.

events.arc: The Cave of the Red Centipede
events.text: Deep in the cave the moss glows red on the walls. Above you on the ceiling, longer than three men, the centipede is asleep: a thousand legs folded, a head like a lacquered helmet, the poison claws twitching in some dream.

choices.text: Scatter realgar and pick the moss slowly

effects.log: The stink fills the cave. The centipede twitches and draws back into a crack in the ceiling. You fill your bag with moss, every step on a path of yellow powder.

choices.text: Pick the moss fast and run

ok.log: Moss in the bag, out of the cave, before it wakes. Behind you, in the dark, a thousand legs rustle like rain on leaves.

fail.deathCause: the red centipede of the southern cave
fail.log: It wakes. It comes down the wall like a red river. Its claws find your leg as you dive through the cave mouth. The leg burns for a month.

choices.text: Leave the moss and back out

effects.log: The centipede shifts in its sleep. You back away along the tunnel, step by step, without the moss and without regrets.

events.arc: The Cave of the Red Centipede
events.text: The alchemist has made a Red Dragon Pill from the moss, and gives you one, warm and red. 'To the one who came out of the cave.' It smells of fire and iron.

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: Fire runs through your meridians like a red river. It burns away an old blockage you had given up on. You lie on the floor gasping and grinning.

choices.text: Sell it to a sect elder

effects.log: The elder pays three times what the alchemist paid you for the moss, and asks no questions.

choices.text: Give it back and ask for a lesson in alchemy

effects.log: The alchemist laughs, and teaches you how the moss was ground, and why, for a whole afternoon.

events.arc: The Python of the Herb Marsh
events.text: Herb-gatherers in the southern marsh will not go near the old banyan island at the marsh's heart. A python lives there, they say, as thick as a water jar, and the thousand-year lingzhi that grows on the banyan roots is its own.

choices.text: Ask how the python hunts

effects.log: 'It waits in the water by the roots. Only its eyes show. It does not bite. It holds.' The gatherer shivers. 'It holds until you stop breathing.'

choices.text: Go and look from a distance

effects.log: From a boat at the edge of the reeds you see the banyan island, the lingzhi glowing on the roots like a lamp, and two eyes in the water, watching you.

choices.text: Leave the lingzhi to the python

effects.log: The gatherers nod approvingly. Some things are not worth it. You are almost certain this is one of them.

events.arc: The Python of the Herb Marsh
events.text: The banyan island at the heart of the marsh. The lingzhi is within reach, on a root above the black water. Two eyes rise out of the water an arm's length away, and a coil as thick as a water jar slides over the root behind you.

choices.text: Grab the lingzhi and leap for the boat

ok.log: Lingzhi in hand, a leap, a splash. The boat rocks. Behind you the python strikes the empty root like a falling tree.

fail.deathCause: the python of the herb marsh
fail.log: The coil closes round your legs and drags you under. You fight in the black water until it lets go, and come up with your ribs cracked.

choices.text: Stand still and let it decide

effects.log: It looks at you for a long time. Then it slides back into the water. You take nothing and row away, very slowly, never taking your eyes from the water.

choices.text: Leave a gift of fish on the root and take only a sliver

effects.log: A basket of fish. The python takes the fish. You take a sliver of the lingzhi, the size of a fingernail, and go.

events.arc: The Python of the Herb Marsh
events.text: Hunters from the city have come to the marsh to kill the python for its skin. They want a guide to the banyan island. They offer good silver.

choices.text: Refuse, and warn the python's island away from them

effects.log: You lead them in circles round the reeds for a day until they give up. The python, you hope, never knows.

choices.text: Guide them, and let them learn

effects.log: They reach the island. Three hunters go in. Two come out, very fast, without their spears. They do not ask for a guide again.

choices.text: Fight the hunters' leader for the marsh

ok.log: The leader goes into the marsh mud and comes up a much humbler hunter. They leave.

fail.deathCause: hunters in the herb marsh
fail.log: They are many and well armed. You are beaten and left in the reeds.

events.arc: The Chain Bridge Over the Abyss
events.text: The only way to the hermit's peak is across a bridge of thirteen iron chains over a gorge so deep the river at the bottom is silent. The planks were taken off years ago. The chains are old. One of them, the woodcutter says, is rusted almost through.

choices.text: Ask which chain is rusted

effects.log: 'The third from the left,' he says. 'Or the fourth. My grandfather knew.' He shrugs. 'Nobody has crossed since.'

choices.text: Look at the chains closely from the near side

effects.log: The third from the left is brown and swollen at the middle, where the spray from the gorge keeps it wet. You will not touch it.

choices.text: Turn back

effects.log: The hermit's peak will be there next year, and the year after. So will you, with any luck.

events.arc: The Chain Bridge Over the Abyss
events.text: Halfway across the chain bridge, in a gusting wind, the chains sway like the strings of a harp. The far side is very far. A chain under your foot gives a long groaning creak.

choices.text: Run the rest of the way

ok.log: You run across the chains like a squirrel along a branch. Behind you a chain snaps with a sound like a bell and falls into the silence.

fail.deathCause: a fall from the chain bridge
fail.log: The chain under you parts. You fall, and catch another, and hang over the abyss by one hand until you can drag yourself up.

choices.text: Move your weight to the chains you checked

effects.log: Not the third, not the fourth. You step across, chain to chain, slow as a heron. The groan stops.

choices.text: Turn round and edge back

effects.log: Back the way you came, inch by inch, with the wind trying to pick you off. You reach the near side and lie on the rock for an hour.

events.arc: The Chain Bridge Over the Abyss
events.text: On the far side, the hermit's peak: a hut, a pine, and an old hermit drinking tea who looks at you with mild interest. 'Nobody has crossed in thirty years,' the hermit says. 'What took you so long?'

choices.text: Ask to be taught

effects.log: The hermit teaches you one thing, over three days: how to stand on nothing. It sounds like a riddle. On the third day, it is not.

choices.text: Offer to mend the bridge

effects.log: The hermit laughs. 'Then people would come.' But lets you replace the third chain, and the fourth, with new iron carried across on your back.

choices.text: Drink tea, and say nothing

effects.log: You drink tea with the hermit until the sun goes down. It is the best tea you have ever had. You cross back the next morning without fear.

events.text: A small sect on a hill keeps a library of three thousand scrolls in a wooden pavilion, the work of twelve generations. The old librarian complains to you over tea that the young disciples keep reading by candlelight in the stacks.

choices.text: Suggest they read in the courtyard by day

effects.log: The librarian beams. The disciples groan. A notice goes up: NO FLAMES IN THE STACKS. The disciples read it by candlelight.

choices.text: Ask which scrolls matter most

effects.log: The librarian takes you to a locked shelf at the back: the founders' own hands, the sect's first manuals, a map of the hill's springs. 'If ever there is a fire, these.'

choices.text: Read in the stacks yourself, by daylight

effects.log: You spend a week reading. The librarian approves of you enormously and lets you borrow a scroll on breathing.

events.text: Night. The bell. The library pavilion is burning: an upper window full of orange light, smoke pouring from the eaves, disciples running with buckets that are far too small. The old librarian is trying to go in.

choices.text: Go in for the founders' shelf

ok.log: Through the smoke to the back shelf, an armful of the oldest scrolls, out through a window as the roof beams fall. The librarian holds them like children.

fail.deathCause: the library fire
fail.log: A burning shelf comes down across the aisle. You get out with the scrolls and your back blistered, choking.

choices.text: Hold the librarian back

effects.log: The old librarian fights you, weeping. You do not let go. The pavilion roof falls in. The librarian will live to rebuild it.

choices.text: Organise a bucket line from the well to the eaves

effects.log: Forty disciples in two lines. The fire is kept off the next pavilion. The library is lost. The sect is not.

choices.text: Go straight to the back window by the locked shelf

effects.log: You know where it is. You break the back window, reach in, and pull out the founders' scrolls without ever going into the smoke.

events.text: The library is rebuilt in stone. The librarian, very old now, asks you to come and see it: three hundred scrolls, the ones that were saved, and blank shelves for the rest. 'We will copy them all from memory,' the librarian says. 'It will take twelve more generations.'

choices.text: Copy one scroll yourself, from memory

effects.log: The breathing scroll you once borrowed. You write it out over a month. It goes on the shelf with your name in the margin, small.

choices.text: Donate silver for paper and ink

effects.log: Paper, ink, brushes, for a generation of copying.

choices.text: Ask what started the fire

effects.log: A candle in the stacks. The librarian smiles sadly. 'A child reading too late. A good child. That child is the head copyist now.'

events.arc: The Escort Who Sold the Route
events.text: You are hired as an extra blade for an escort agency carrying a strongbox to the provincial capital. The escort captain is cheerful and competent. The second-in-command, Wei, keeps asking which road you think the captain will take.

choices.text: Tell Wei you do not know

effects.log: Wei smiles and drops it. That evening you see Wei talking with a pedlar who leaves the inn before dawn, riding fast.

choices.text: Tell the captain about Wei's questions

effects.log: The captain laughs. 'Wei has been with me eleven years.' But the captain changes the road the next morning, without telling anyone.

choices.text: Keep your eyes open and say nothing

effects.log: You watch everyone. Everyone watches the strongbox. The road is long.

events.arc: The Escort Who Sold the Route
events.text: In a narrow valley the escort is surrounded: thirty masked riders, waiting exactly where the road was supposed to go. Wei has drawn a sword, and is standing beside the masked leader, and will not look at the captain.

choices.text: Fight to hold the strongbox

ok.log: The escort closes round the strongbox and you cut through toward Wei. The riders break when Wei falls back. The box is saved.

fail.deathCause: the ambush on the escort road
fail.log: Too many riders. You go down defending the box and wake to find it gone, the captain wounded, and Wei gone with it.

choices.text: Call out to Wei by name, in front of everyone

effects.log: 'Eleven years, Wei.' The masked riders look at Wei. Wei hesitates for one breath too long and the captain is on Wei like a tiger. The riders, leaderless, pull back.

choices.text: Fall back with the wounded and let the box go

effects.log: The box goes. The people do not. The captain, bleeding, says it was the right call and will say so to the agency.

choices.text: You knew the road would change: they are waiting for nothing

effects.log: The masked riders wait in the wrong valley. You hear about it at the capital, where the strongbox arrives on time.

events.arc: The Escort Who Sold the Route
events.text: Wei has been seen in a border town, rich, with a new name. The escort captain asks you to come and bring Wei back for the agency's judgement. 'Alive,' the captain says. 'I want to ask why.'

choices.text: Bring Wei back alive

ok.log: Wei fights, then does not. On the road back Wei talks: a debt, a sick child, a threat. The captain listens. The judgement is exile, not death.

fail.deathCause: Wei's bodyguards in the border town
fail.log: Wei has bodyguards now. You get out of the border town with a wound and without Wei.

choices.text: Find out why first, before you go

effects.log: A gambling debt. A brother held as surety. You tell the captain. The captain goes alone, in the end, and comes back without Wei, and does not speak of it.

choices.text: Refuse: you were hired for one road

effects.log: The captain nods. 'Fair.' Someone else goes. You never hear what happens.

events.arc: The Escort Who Sold the Route
events.text: The escort agency offers you a permanent place: your own team, your own banner, a strongbox and a road. The captain, grey now, pours you a cup of tea. 'You can tell when a person is selling a road,' the captain says. 'That is the whole job.'

choices.text: Take the banner

effects.log: Your own team of six, a road to the capital and back, and a captain to report to who trusts you. The pay is good and the stories are better.

choices.text: Decline, but promise to ride when needed

effects.log: You ride twice more with the agency, years apart. Both times the road is sold. Both times you can tell.

choices.text: Ask the captain about Wei

effects.log: 'Writes to me,' the captain says. 'From the frontier. Every New Year. Never asks for anything.' The captain looks into the wine. 'I always write back.'

events.arc: The Witness and the Eastern Depot
events.text: At an inn by the canal, a frightened clerk from the salt office begs you for help. The clerk saw something: a eunuch of the Eastern Depot, the emperor's secret police, taking a bribe to let a smuggler fleet pass. Now the Depot is looking for the clerk.

choices.text: Hide the clerk in your room

effects.log: The clerk spends the night under your bed, shaking. At midnight, footsteps in the corridor stop outside your door, and then go on.

choices.text: Ask what the clerk can prove

effects.log: A ledger page, copied in the clerk's own hand, with the eunuch's seal. The clerk holds it out with both hands like a live coal.

choices.text: Tell the clerk to run, and give silver for the road

effects.log: The clerk takes the silver and runs south. You hope it is far enough. With the Depot it never is.

events.arc: The Witness and the Eastern Depot
events.text: The Eastern Depot comes to the inn at dawn: a dozen men in brown with embroidered boots, and a smiling eunuch with a white face who asks, very politely, whether you have seen a clerk from the salt office.

choices.text: Lie, politely

effects.log: You lie as well as you have ever lied. The eunuch smiles and smiles. The men search the inn and find nothing, because the clerk is in the canal under the jetty, breathing through a reed.

choices.text: Fight your way out with the clerk

ok.log: Through the back, over the canal wall, into a boat. The Depot's men are good. You are better, today. The clerk is with you, alive.

fail.deathCause: the Eastern Depot's men at the canal inn
fail.log: The Depot's men are very good. You are cut down on the jetty and the clerk is taken. You wake in a ditch, left for dead.

choices.text: Say you know nothing, and mean it, and let them search

effects.log: You do not know where the clerk is. That is the truth, and the eunuch, who has heard a great many lies, can taste the difference. They go.

events.arc: The Witness and the Eastern Depot
events.text: The ledger page with the eunuch's seal must reach the Censorate in the capital, the only office the Depot fears. Every road there is watched. The clerk cannot go. Someone else must.

choices.text: Carry it yourself, by the back roads

ok.log: Twenty days of back roads, wrong turns, a river swum at night. You hand the page to a censor in a plain grey office. The censor reads it and goes very still.

fail.deathCause: the Eastern Depot's hunters
fail.log: They catch you at the last gate. You escape into the city with an arrow in your back and the page soaked in your sweat, and deliver it, and collapse.

choices.text: Send it hidden in a merchant's bale of silk

effects.log: The merchant never knows. The silk goes to the capital. The page goes to the Censorate, by a friend of a friend. It is slow. It works.

choices.text: Burn it, and tell the clerk to disappear

effects.log: Some fights are too big. The clerk weeps, and agrees, and goes into a monastery in the west under a new name. The eunuch is never punished.

events.arc: The Witness and the Eastern Depot
events.text: News from the capital: the eunuch with the white face has been stripped of rank by the Censorate and sent to sweep an imperial tomb. The clerk from the salt office is promoted. A letter comes for you with no seal and no name.

choices.text: Read the letter

effects.log: Two characters: Thank you. And under them, smaller: Burn this. You burn it, and smile all day.

choices.text: Leave the province anyway

effects.log: The Depot has a long memory. You go west for a few years. Nothing ever happens. You are glad you went.

choices.text: Visit the clerk at the new office

effects.log: The clerk stands up so fast the inkstone falls. You have a cup of tea in a very small, very honest office. Neither of you says why.

events.text: In a town you have never visited, people bow to you in the street, or spit. A swordsman calling himself by your name has been here: challenged the local master, won, and taken a 'tribute' from every shop. He left a month ago, heading north.

choices.text: Pay back the shopkeepers yourself

effects.log: Out of your own purse, door to door. The shopkeepers are baffled. One of them, an old woman, says: 'The other one did not look like you at all.'

choices.text: Ask what the impostor looked like

effects.log: Tall, a scar on the chin, a sword with a red tassel, laughs too loudly. Fights well. The local master is still in bed.

choices.text: Shrug and move on

effects.log: Names are just names. Then, in the next town, a sect elder refuses to see you because of what 'you' did to their disciple.

events.text: The local master the impostor beat has sent two senior disciples to find you, 'the one who shamed our hall'. They stop you at a bridge, swords out. Behind them a crowd is gathering to watch.

choices.text: Describe the impostor's scar and tassel

effects.log: The disciples look at your chin, and your plain sword, and at each other. One of them lowers the sword slowly. 'We will tell our master.'

choices.text: Fight them, but do not harm them

ok.log: You take both swords away without a cut on anyone and hand them back hilt first. The crowd is impressed. The disciples are confused. That is enough.

fail.deathCause: a duel at the bridge over a stolen name
fail.log: They are better than you hoped and angrier. You leave the bridge with a cut across the ribs and a very bad reputation.

choices.text: Kneel, and offer to go to their master

effects.log: Kneeling in front of a crowd is hard. You do it. The disciples, astonished, take you to their master, who takes one look and says: 'No. That is not the one.'

events.text: Up in the north, in a market town, a tall swordsman with a scar on the chin and a red tassel on the sword is drinking in the best inn, loudly, under your name.

choices.text: Challenge the impostor in front of the whole inn

ok.log: The impostor is good. You are better. In the end the impostor is sitting on the floor, and the whole inn knows whose name it is.

fail.deathCause: a duel with the impostor in the north
fail.log: The impostor is better than good. You lose, in front of everyone, to someone using your name. The irony is not lost on anyone.

choices.text: Sit down at the impostor's table and say who you are

effects.log: The impostor laughs, then sees you are serious, then goes white. The inn goes quiet. The impostor leaves by the back door and is not seen again.

choices.text: Tell the town magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate's constables arrest the impostor for the tribute money. The impostor shouts your name all the way to the cell.

events.text: A letter comes, months later, from the impostor, in a surprisingly good hand: 'I used your name because it was the only name anyone feared. I am sorry. I have a name of my own now. I am trying to make it worth something.'

choices.text: Write back with advice

effects.log: You write: Pay back the shops. Then fight only people who want to fight. A year later, a second letter: Done. Both. Thank you.

choices.text: Laugh, and keep the letter

effects.log: It is the strangest compliment you have ever been paid. You keep it in your pack for years.

choices.text: Ask around for the impostor's new name

effects.log: A young swordsman in the north, it seems, of growing fame and good manners. Nobody knows the scar's history. You keep it to yourself.

events.arc: The Miasma Valley of the South
events.text: In the far south the road goes through a valley that fills each afternoon with a green-white mist, sweet-smelling. Your guide, a woman of the hill tribes, chews a bitter leaf and offers you one. 'Chew. Or you sleep in the valley and do not wake.'

choices.text: Chew the bitter leaf

effects.log: It is the most bitter thing you have ever tasted. Your eyes water all the way through the valley. The mist smells sweet and you do not want to lie down in it.

choices.text: Ask what the mist is

effects.log: 'The breath of the valley. Rotting flowers, old water, things that died.' She spits. 'The southern miasma. It has killed armies.'

choices.text: Refuse: you will hold your breath with qi

effects.log: She laughs and shrugs. 'Your army.' You decide to hurry.

events.arc: The Miasma Valley of the South
events.text: The afternoon mist rolls into the valley earlier than the guide said. It is sweet, and warm, and your legs are heavy. Ahead, a merchant and his mule have already lain down by the road, smiling, asleep.

choices.text: Drag the merchant out with you

ok.log: You haul the merchant over your shoulders and stagger uphill out of the mist. The mule follows on its own. On the ridge the merchant wakes, weeping.

fail.deathCause: the miasma of the southern valley
fail.log: Halfway up the slope your own legs fold. You lie down in the sweet mist with the merchant until the guide comes back with a wet cloth over her face.

choices.text: Chew the leaf and walk on, steady

effects.log: The bitterness keeps your head clear. You walk through the mist, and back, with the merchant's mule, and the guide brings the merchant.

choices.text: Turn back uphill, fast, and shout for the guide

effects.log: You climb out of the mist with your head spinning. The guide goes down with a cloth over her face and comes back with the merchant, cursing everyone.

events.arc: The Miasma Valley of the South
events.text: The hill-tribe guide takes you to her village, where the bitter leaf grows in terraces, and the old women grind it into a paste for travellers. 'The lowland healers do not know it,' she says. 'They never ask.'

choices.text: Ask to learn how it is made

effects.log: The old women laugh at you all week and teach you anyway. You leave with a jar of paste and a recipe nobody in the lowlands has.

choices.text: Buy a sack of leaves to take north

effects.log: The lowland healers are suspicious, then astonished. Within a year, the miasma road is safer for everyone.

choices.text: Thank the guide, and go

effects.log: She shrugs and chews a leaf. 'Come back when you need to cross again.' You do, twice.

events.text: In the hill villages, a new cult is spreading: the Pure Moon Society, who promise that at the next blood moon their followers will be lifted up into immortality. A widow says her son has joined. He gave them the family's land.

choices.text: Go to one of their meetings

effects.log: Lanterns, chanting, a beautiful preacher in white. Everyone drinks from a silver bowl. You pretend to. It smells of sweet incense and something sour that makes your head swim.

choices.text: Ask where the blood moon rite will be held

effects.log: The widow does not know. A child does: the old quarry above the river, where the Society has been building something in the dark.

choices.text: Tell the county magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate laughs. Cults come and go. 'Let them sing to the moon.'

events.text: The blood moon. In the old quarry, two hundred followers in white are standing in a ring at the edge of a great pit. The preacher is chanting. The followers have drunk from the silver bowl and are swaying. At the climax they will step forward. Into the pit.

choices.text: Break the rite: attack the preacher

ok.log: The preacher has guards, and the guards fall, and the preacher falls, and the chanting stops. The followers wake slowly, as if from a dream, at the very edge.

fail.deathCause: the Pure Moon rite in the quarry
fail.log: The guards are good and the followers, dreaming, close round you to protect their preacher. You are pushed into the pit and climb out by morning, broken.

choices.text: Knock over the bowls and shout the truth

effects.log: You know what was in the bowls. You shout it. Some of the followers hear you, and stop, and hold on to their neighbours. Fewer step forward. Not none.

choices.text: Pull the widow's son out of the ring

effects.log: You find him by his mother's description and drag him back from the edge. He fights you, dreaming, and then sleeps in your arms. One saved. You could not stop the rest.

choices.text: Light the quarry with signal fires for the county soldiers

effects.log: Your fires on the quarry rim bring the soldiers you warned a week ago, who did not believe you, and now do. They stop it at the edge.

events.text: The Pure Moon Society is broken. The preacher, it turns out, was selling the followers' land to a salt merchant. The followers have come down from the quarry with nothing, ashamed, and the villages will not take them back.

choices.text: Speak for them to the villages

effects.log: You stand in each village square in turn and say: they were fooled, as you would have been. Slowly, one by one, families open their doors.

choices.text: Go after the land for them

effects.log: A month of magistrates and ledgers. The salt merchant gives most of the land back rather than explain to the Censorate how it was bought.

choices.text: Take the widow's son home

effects.log: His mother holds him at the gate. He cannot speak. He works her fields for the rest of her life.

events.text: Years later, in another province, you hear of a new society that promises immortality at the next blood moon. The preacher is said to be beautiful, dressed in white, and to have a silver bowl.

choices.text: Go, at once

effects.log: You know the shape of it now. This time you are at the first meeting, not the last. The society does not last a season.

choices.text: Write to the magistrate of that province, in detail

effects.log: The silver bowl, the sour drink, the pit, the salt merchant. This magistrate believes you. The society is broken before the moon.

choices.text: Send the widow's son to warn them

effects.log: He goes, very quiet, and stands up in the first meeting and tells his story. People listen to him. They would not have listened to you.

events.text: Two sects have been feuding over a river valley for a year. You are passing through. In the inn, the disciples of the Azure Wave sit on one side and the disciples of the Iron Ridge on the other, and both sides keep looking at you, a stranger with a sword.

choices.text: Sit exactly in the middle

effects.log: Both sides glare at you. Nobody starts anything with a stranger in the way. The innkeeper brings you free dumplings in gratitude.

choices.text: Listen to both sides' grievances

effects.log: A dam, a dead goat, an insult at a wedding twenty years ago. It is all very stupid, and somebody's brother died last month.

choices.text: Leave the inn and the valley

effects.log: You walk out. Behind you, through the door, you hear a stool hit a wall.

events.text: On the valley road, the feud boils over: thirty disciples of each side, in a line, swords drawn, on either side of a ford. You are standing in the middle of the ford with water to your knees.

choices.text: Stand your ground and order them both to stop

ok.log: You have a voice that carries. Both lines hesitate. Both leaders come forward into the ford to shout at you, which means they are talking.

fail.deathCause: the sect feud at the ford
fail.log: They charge anyway. You are caught in the middle of sixty swords. You stagger out of the ford downstream, cut in a dozen places.

choices.text: Get out of the ford and let them fight

effects.log: You wade out and stand on the bank. It is a short, savage, stupid fight. Three dead. Nobody wins.

choices.text: Name the dam and the goat and the wedding, loudly

effects.log: Both lines have heard their own grievances shouted by a stranger and they sound absurd. Someone laughs. The swords go down.

events.text: The two sect leaders sit at a table in the inn, with you between them, very uncomfortable. They need a judge they both distrust equally. You are it.

choices.text: Divide the river and the dam fairly

effects.log: A whole day of shouting. A line on a map. Two seals. The feud ends, for now. Both sects send you gifts and complain about the line forever.

choices.text: Make them repair the dam together

effects.log: Thirty disciples from each sect, one dam, one summer. By autumn some of them are friends. One pair marries.

choices.text: Refuse to judge: it is their river

effects.log: They are offended. Then they are left alone at the table. After an hour, they start talking.

events.arc: The House With an Old Array
events.text: You are offered a fine old courtyard house very cheap. The broker shrugs at the price. 'Nobody stays more than a month. Bad dreams. Cold spots.' In the courtyard, the paving stones are laid in an odd, spiralling pattern.

choices.text: Study the paving pattern

effects.log: It is an array: old, faded, half the stones moved by gardeners. It was meant to protect the house. It has been broken. Broken arrays do strange things.

choices.text: Rent it for a month

effects.log: The dreams start on the third night: a fire, a family, a door that will not open. The cold spot is by the well.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: The broker sighs. The house stays empty another year.

events.arc: The House With an Old Array
events.text: Night in the old house. The array has woken: the courtyard stones are glowing faintly, the air is thick, and the well is pulling at you, slowly, like a hand on your sleeve. In the dream-light a door is burning that is not there.

choices.text: Resist the pull and walk out of the gate

ok.log: Step by step, against the pull, as if wading through deep water. At the gate the pull lets go. You sit on the step till dawn.

fail.deathCause: a broken array in an old house
fail.log: The pull wins. You wake at the bottom of the dry well with a broken arm, looking up at the stars.

choices.text: Move one stone back into its place

effects.log: You know which one. You drag it across the courtyard, against the pull, and drop it into its hole. The glow stops. The house sighs like a sleeper turning over.

choices.text: Hold on to the gatepost until dawn

effects.log: All night with your arms round the gatepost, the well pulling, the burning door. At dawn, it stops. You let go and fall over.

events.arc: The House With an Old Array
events.text: In the house's old records at the county office: a family burned in this house a hundred years ago, trapped behind a door that an array meant to protect them had locked. The array has been trying to open that door ever since.

choices.text: Restore the whole array properly

effects.log: A month of moving stones and redrawing lines. When it is done, the house is warm, the dreams are gone, and the well is only a well.

choices.text: Hold a rite for the family

effects.log: Incense, paper money, the family's names read from the record. The cold spot by the well is gone the next morning.

choices.text: Buy the house now that you know

effects.log: The broker cannot believe it. You live there years. It is the quietest house you have ever known.
