events.text: The lake rose when the new dam was built downstream, and drowned a river shrine. Fishermen say that on still nights you can hear its bell under the water, and that the ones who go down to look for its gold do not come up.

choices.text: Ask who went down

effects.log: Three young men, one each year, on the anniversary of the drowning. 'The bell calls them,' says an old fisherman. 'Like a mother calling.'

choices.text: Go out on the lake at night to listen

effects.log: Very faint, under the boat: a bell. A slow one. You row home without looking into the water.

choices.text: Laugh at the story

effects.log: The fishermen do not laugh. One of them lost a son that way.

events.text: The anniversary of the drowning. A young fisherman is rowing out to the middle of the lake with a stone tied to a rope, to go down. His eyes are fixed and strange. The bell is ringing under the water.

choices.text: Dive after him when he goes over

ok.log: Black water, cold, the rope. You find him at the bottom by the drowned shrine gate and haul him up by the hair. On the surface he wakes, screaming, and then weeping.

fail.deathCause: the drowned shrine under the lake
fail.log: The cold and the dark and the bell. You get him to the surface, and your own lungs give out. Fishermen drag you both into a boat.

choices.text: Cut the rope before he jumps

effects.log: You row alongside and cut the rope with one stroke. He jumps anyway, and floats, bewildered, and you pull him in.

choices.text: Ring a bell of your own, louder

effects.log: You bang the boat's iron pot like a bell, over and over. The young man blinks, the strange look goes out of his eyes, and he drops the stone.

events.text: The fishermen want to bring up the shrine's bell, so it stops calling. It is far down, and heavy, and the water is cold.

choices.text: Dive and tie the ropes to the bell

ok.log: Three dives. The ropes on. Thirty fishermen haul. The bell comes up out of the lake streaming green weed, and is hung in a new shrine on the shore.

fail.deathCause: the drowned shrine under the lake
fail.log: On the third dive your foot catches in the shrine's drowned gate. You are pulled free by the rope, half drowned.

choices.text: Hold a rite on the shore for the drowned

effects.log: The three young men's names, read over the water. The bell stops ringing that night and never rings again.

choices.text: Build a new shrine on the shore and leave the bell

effects.log: A small shrine on the bank, with a new bell. On still nights now, the new bell answers the old one, and nobody goes down.

events.text: Under Black Mountain, three hundred years ago, the righteous sects sealed a demonic master in the rock with nine iron spikes and nine monks' lives. Lately the springs around the mountain run warm and red with iron, and the birds have left. An old monk at the mountain's foot temple says the seal is weakening.

choices.text: Ask how the seal works

effects.log: Nine spikes, nine sutras, renewed every century by a master of the first rank. 'The last renewal was due ninety years ago,' the monk says. 'Nobody came.'

choices.text: Go up to see the spikes

effects.log: Nine iron spikes in a ring on a bare summit, each as thick as a temple pillar. Three are cracked. One has a hairline crack that is glowing red, faintly, like a coal under ash.

choices.text: Send word to the great sects

effects.log: Letters to the sects. Polite replies. Nobody comes. The great sects are busy with each other.

events.text: On the summit of Black Mountain at midnight, a second spike cracks with a sound like a temple bell breaking. Out of the crack pours a black wind that smells of rust and cold ash, and in the wind a voice, delighted, laughing, very close.

choices.text: Drive your own qi into the cracked spikes

ok.log: You pour your qi into the iron like water into a cracked jar. The red glow dims. The laughing voice stops, and swears, and goes quiet.

fail.deathCause: the demon sealed under Black Mountain
fail.log: The voice reaches through the crack and into your meridians. You are thrown off the summit in a storm of black wind and wake on the slope below with your qi in tatters.

choices.text: Chant the nine sutras with the old monk

effects.log: The old monk climbed after you. Together, all night, the nine sutras, over and over. At dawn the black wind sinks back into the crack.

choices.text: Retreat down the mountain and raise the alarm

effects.log: You run. Behind you the laughter follows, then fades. At the foot temple the monks ring every bell they have.

events.text: Something has come out of the crack: not the demon, but its shadow, a thing of black wind in the shape of a man, walking down the mountain toward the villages, and where it walks the grass dies.

choices.text: Meet the shadow on the mountain road

ok.log: It fights like a memory of a master. You cut it apart, again and again, until at dawn there is nothing left but a smell of cold ash and a burned circle on the road.

fail.deathCause: the demon's shadow from Black Mountain
fail.log: It goes through you like cold water. You wake in a field of dead grass, and the shadow has gone on, to the next village.

choices.text: Lead the villagers to the foot temple

effects.log: The temple is warded. The shadow walks round it all night, and cannot enter. At dawn it fades back up the mountain.

choices.text: Hold a torch and a sutra at the village gate

effects.log: Fire and scripture. The shadow stands at the gate, waiting, until dawn, and then turns away. Something in you is very cold for weeks.

events.text: The seal must be renewed, properly, by a master of your strength, with nine new spikes of black iron and nine days of chanting on the summit without sleep. The great sects have finally sent help: one young disciple, and an apology.

choices.text: Renew the seal yourself

ok.log: Nine days. Nine spikes. Nine sutras, until your voice is gone. On the ninth night the laughing in the rock stops. The springs run clear.

fail.deathCause: renewing the seal under Black Mountain
fail.log: On the seventh day you fall asleep. The black wind comes through you for an instant. The young disciple finishes the chant over your body.

choices.text: Teach the young disciple to do it, and stand guard

effects.log: Nine days of teaching on a summit. The disciple is clumsy, then good. The seal is renewed by two, and the second one will be able to do it again.

choices.text: Ask the foot temple's monks to share the nine days

effects.log: Nine monks, one each day, in turn. You hold the spikes. It takes longer. Nobody dies. That was the point.

events.text: A century on, by the old monk's reckoning, someone will have to renew the seal again. At the foot temple, the old monk asks what to write in the records.

choices.text: Write how it was done, step by step

effects.log: Every spike, every sutra, every mistake. Somebody a hundred years from now will read it by lamplight and be grateful.

choices.text: Write the names of everyone who helped

effects.log: The monks, the young disciple, the villagers who held torches. Not your own. The old monk adds yours anyway.

choices.text: Write: do not wait ninety years this time

effects.log: In large characters, on the first page. The old monk laughs until coughing.

events.text: A star has been growing brighter in the north-east for a month, until now it shows in daylight. The court astronomers say it is an omen. An old hermit on the mountain says it is a stone, falling, and that it will land in the valley of the Three Rivers.

choices.text: Go to the Three Rivers valley to warn the villages

effects.log: Most laugh. Some leave. The headman of the largest village moves the children up into the hills, just in case.

choices.text: Ask the hermit how he knows

effects.log: Twenty years of watching, a hundred sheets of reckoning. The numbers are very clear. 'In nine days,' the hermit says. 'At dusk.'

choices.text: Watch it from the mountain

effects.log: Every night it is larger. On the last night it has a tail like a burning horse.

events.text: Dusk in the Three Rivers valley. The star is a second sun, white and screaming, falling. The ground is shaking. In the village below you, people are still standing in the street, looking up.

choices.text: Run down and drive them out of the valley

ok.log: You run through the village shouting. People run. When the star strikes the far end of the valley, the wave of air knocks everyone flat in the hills, alive.

fail.deathCause: the falling star in the Three Rivers valley
fail.log: The blast catches you in the open. You are thrown across a field and wake with the valley on fire around you.

choices.text: Shout from the hill, and let them come to you

effects.log: Your voice carries a long way. Many come. Not all. When the star strikes, the hill shakes under you like a drum.

choices.text: You knew the hour: they left at noon

effects.log: The headman moved everyone at noon, because you told him the hour. At dusk the valley is empty when the star comes down.

events.text: In the Three Rivers valley there is a new lake, perfectly round, and in the middle of it, steaming, a black stone the size of a house. Sects are already arriving to claim it: meteor iron, the finest sword metal there is.

choices.text: Claim a piece for yourself before the sects fight

ok.log: You wade in first, cut a piece as long as your arm, and wade out with it under the eyes of five sects, none of whom dare stop you.

fail.deathCause: sect fighting over the star iron
fail.log: Three sects decide you are the first enemy. You get out of the lake with a piece and a dozen wounds.

choices.text: Make the sects share it fairly

effects.log: A day of shouting. A rope round the stone, divided in sections. You are given a section as judge's fee.

choices.text: Insist the village gets the first share

effects.log: The village lost its fields. The sects grumble and pay the village in silver for its iron. The village rebuilds in the hills.

events.arc: The Flood Dragon of Lake Dongting
events.text: The fishermen of the great lake say a jiao, a flood dragon, sleeps in its deepest part, and wakes every sixty years in the rains to try to swim down the river to the sea and become a true dragon. When it wakes, the lake rises and the river towns drown. The sixtieth year is this one.

choices.text: Listen to the oldest fisherman

effects.log: Sixty years ago, he was a boy. He saw it: a back like a capsized boat, horns like dead trees. 'It does not want to hurt anyone,' he says. 'It only wants the sea. We are in the way.'

choices.text: Help the towns raise their dykes

effects.log: A season of earth and baskets and shouting overseers. The dykes are a head higher. Nobody knows if it will be enough.

choices.text: Doubt the story

effects.log: A lake that rises in the rains. Of course. You stay on the lake road. The sky in the south is a strange dark green.

events.arc: The Flood Dragon of Lake Dongting
events.text: The rains. The great lake is rising a hand an hour, and in the middle of it the water is heaving, and something vast breaks the surface, and roars, and the roar shakes the tiles off the roofs of the lake towns.

choices.text: Go out on the lake and fight it

ok.log: On a boat, then on its back, then in the water, all night. At dawn it sinks back into the deep, wounded, and the lake falls. You crawl ashore with a scale as big as a shield.

fail.deathCause: the flood dragon of Lake Dongting
fail.log: It throws your boat into the air like a leaf. You wake on a dyke a li away with the lake around your waist.

choices.text: Get the towns onto the dykes and the hills

effects.log: All night, boats and ropes and carts, the old carried, the children carried. When the lake comes over the lowest town, the town is empty.

choices.text: Open the old sluice so it can reach the river

effects.log: The old fisherman said it only wants the sea. You and a hundred men open the sluice to the river. The jiao smells the current, turns, and goes for it.

events.arc: The Flood Dragon of Lake Dongting
events.text: The jiao is in the river, swimming for the sea, and the river towns lie in its path: forty li of houses on the banks. Ahead of it, a great stone bridge spans the river. It will not pass under it. It will go through it.

choices.text: Stand on the bridge and turn it aside

ok.log: You meet it on the bridge. It meets you. For a moment you hold the eye of a creature older than any sect, and it turns, roaring, and passes beside the bridge, and the bridge stands.

fail.deathCause: the flood dragon on the river
fail.log: The bridge goes. So do you, into the flood, with its wake throwing you down the river like a twig.

choices.text: Clear the bridge and the banks before it comes

effects.log: You run ahead of it, shouting. The bridge falls. Nobody is on it.

choices.text: Open every weir on the way so it can pass easily

effects.log: Weir after weir, opened ahead of it. The jiao passes through the river towns like a great slow ship, and the towns watch from the roofs.

events.arc: The Flood Dragon of Lake Dongting
events.text: On the coast, a fisherman says something came down the river into the sea three months ago, and lay in the shallows for a day, and then the sky opened and a dragon went up into the clouds, golden, roaring, and was gone.

choices.text: Go and stand on the shore where it rose

effects.log: The sand is glassy in a long line, as if a lightning bolt had lain there. You stand on it, and feel something vast and grateful, very far off.

choices.text: Return to the lake towns and help them rebuild

effects.log: They are already rebuilding, on stilts this time. Sixty years from now, the jiao's child will wake in the lake, and they will be ready.

choices.text: Tell the old fisherman of the lake

effects.log: He weeps, at ninety, sitting on his doorstep. 'It got to the sea,' he says. 'After all this time.' You both sit there till dark.

events.arc: The Blood Moon League's First Blade
events.text: A list is circulating in the dark trade: the Blood Moon League has named its targets for the year, the masters it will kill to prove itself. Your name is fifth. The first four are already dead.

choices.text: Find out how the four died

effects.log: One poisoned in a bath. One at a funeral. One on a ferry. One in bed. All at night, all with a red crescent drawn on the wall in the victim's own ink.

choices.text: Strengthen your defences

effects.log: New locks, a dog, a sleeping place nobody knows. You start to feel like prey. You do not like it.

choices.text: Let it be known you are not afraid

effects.log: You drink openly in the best teahouse in the province every night. You are very afraid.

events.arc: The Blood Moon League's First Blade
events.text: Night. Your ink stone is wet. Someone has used it. On the wall above your bed, in your own ink, someone has begun to draw a red crescent, and stopped halfway, and is standing very still in the dark corner of the room.

choices.text: Strike first, into the dark corner

roll.foeName: the first blade of the Blood Moon

ok.log: Your blade meets a blade. The fight is silent, fast and short, and when it is over the League's first blade is on the floor, and the crescent is still unfinished.

fail.deathCause: the Blood Moon League's first blade
fail.log: The first blade is the best killer you have ever faced. You are cut three times before you get out of the window and into the river.

choices.text: Throw the lamp and dive out of the window

effects.log: Burning oil and broken shutters. You land in the courtyard rolling and run. Behind you, someone curses, very quietly.

choices.text: You knew the pattern: you are not sleeping in this room

effects.log: The assassin finds an empty bed and your dog. You are across the courtyard with a crossbow, watching the window. The League's first blade comes out of it into your sights.

events.arc: The Blood Moon League's First Blade
events.text: The Blood Moon League has lost its first blade. The list is changed in the dark trade. Your name is at the top now: the one they must kill or be laughed at. But the League's founder has sent a letter instead.

choices.text: Read the letter

effects.log: 'You have shamed us. We can kill you, or we can disband. Our honour cannot stand a third choice.' You read it twice. Then you write back: disband.

choices.text: Find the founder and end the League

ok.log: A house by a lotus pond, an old founder in a wheeled chair, twenty killers who will not fight for an old man's honour. The League ends with a signature.

fail.deathCause: the Blood Moon League
fail.log: Twenty killers will fight for their founder after all. You get out by the lotus pond, half dead.

choices.text: Ignore it, and live as you lived

effects.log: You go on drinking in the same teahouse. The League waits a year, then two, then is heard of no more. Fear, it seems, can expire.

events.arc: The Blood Moon League's First Blade
events.text: A young woman comes to your door with a sword wrapped in red cloth: the first blade's sister. She has come to return it, she says. Her brother told her, before, that if he lost to anyone he hoped it would be to someone worth losing to.

choices.text: Take the sword

effects.log: It is a beautiful sword, very light, made for killing in small rooms. You keep it wrapped and never use it. It is a debt, of a kind.

choices.text: Give it back to her

effects.log: 'It is all you have of him,' you say. She looks at you for a long time, and takes it, and bows.

choices.text: Ask about her brother

effects.log: He had a cat. He could not read. He sent all his pay home. You listen until dark. When she goes, you sit in the dark for a long time.

events.text: A peak master you defeated in a public duel years ago sends a gracious letter: an invitation to a reconciliation banquet at the master's mountain hall. The letter is written in a beautiful hand. The mountain hall, a traveller mentions, has been closed to guests for a month while 'masons' worked inside.

choices.text: Accept, and go carefully

effects.log: You go up the mountain with your eyes open. The steps are new. Some of the paving stones in the hall courtyard are a slightly different grey.

choices.text: Send a gift and decline

effects.log: A fine gift, a polite refusal. Another letter comes a month later, more gracious still, and a little impatient.

choices.text: Ask the traveller about the masons

effects.log: Masons from the Array Hall of the south, the traveller says. Expensive ones. The kind who build cages that look like rooms.

events.text: The banquet hall. As you take your seat, the doors close behind you with a soft click, and the floor lights up in lines of blue, and the air thickens like honey. Your host stands up, smiling, outside the array, on the other side of a pane of qi.

choices.text: Break the array by force

ok.log: You hit the weakest line with everything you have. The blue lines crack like ice and the doors burst open. Your host is not smiling any more.

fail.deathCause: the rival peak master's array
fail.log: The array drinks your blow and gives it back. You lie on the hall floor while it presses down, until a disciple of the host, sickened, cuts the anchor stone.

choices.text: Step only on the old grey stones

effects.log: You saw them in the courtyard: the new stones are the array. You step across the hall on the old grey ones, and the blue lines cannot close around you.

choices.text: Sit still and talk to your host

effects.log: You talk, calmly, through the pane of qi, about the old duel, about pride, about the price of southern masons. It takes all night. At dawn your host, ashamed, opens the door.

events.text: The peak master sits in the ruined banquet hall, among the broken stones of the array, and waits for you to decide what to do.

choices.text: Demand a duel, here, now, fairly

ok.log: A fair fight, this time. You win again. The peak master laughs, hollow. 'Twice. Of course.' And bows, at last, properly.

fail.deathCause: a duel in the ruined banquet hall
fail.log: The peak master has been training for this for years. You lose. It is fair. It is also very painful.

choices.text: Walk out and leave your host to it

effects.log: You walk out without a word. Behind you, the sound of someone sitting alone in a hall they built to kill you, for a long time.

choices.text: Tell the peak master's disciples what was done

effects.log: The disciples are horrified. Within a month the peak has a new master. The old master lives quietly in a hut at the foot of the mountain.

events.text: An alchemist of the Hundred Herbs Hall has been burning strange cauldrons on a hill above a city, and the smoke drifts over the rice fields. After the last rain, the frogs in the paddies died, and a farmer's buffalo will not stand.

choices.text: Climb the hill to see the cauldrons

effects.log: Nine cauldrons, green smoke, and the alchemist's servants with cloths over their faces. The alchemist is very charming and very eager for you to leave.

choices.text: Test the rainwater from the paddy

effects.log: You drip it on a leaf. The leaf goes brown in an hour. On your fingertip it stings like a wasp.

choices.text: Tell the city magistrate

effects.log: The magistrate is the alchemist's patient, for a pill that keeps his hair black. Nothing happens.

events.text: Clouds over the city. Then rain, green-tinged, smelling of copper, falling on the markets, the gardens, the people running for doorways. Where it falls on skin, it burns.

choices.text: Climb to the cauldrons and put them out in the rain

ok.log: Up the hill through the burning rain. Nine cauldrons kicked over, one by one, into the mud. The green smoke stops. The rain turns clear by evening.

fail.deathCause: the alchemist's green rain
fail.log: The rain and the smoke together are too much. You collapse among the cauldrons and wake days later in a temple, your skin peeling.

choices.text: Get people under roofs and wash the burns

effects.log: All afternoon, shouting people into doorways, washing burns with clean well water. When the rain stops, nobody in your street is badly hurt.

choices.text: Bring the leaf and the water to the city's healers

effects.log: The healers, with proof in front of them, go to the magistrate in a body. The cauldrons are put out by soldiers before the next cloud.

events.text: The alchemist has fled south with a cauldron and a notebook. The city's rice fields are poisoned for a year. The farmers are desperate.

choices.text: Go after the alchemist

effects.log: A month on the southern roads. You find the alchemist trying the same thing in another city, and the cauldron goes into the river, and the notebook into the fire.

choices.text: Help the farmers flood the paddies to wash them

effects.log: Three floodings, three drainings. By autumn the frogs are back. The farmers plant the next spring.

choices.text: Pay for seed rice from the next province

effects.log: Silver and seed rice, enough for the poorest hundred families.

events.text: Every map of the western mountains has a blank where the Valley of No Return should be. Explorers go in for its spirit herbs and its legend of an immortal's cave. A tea seller at the valley mouth keeps a wall of wooden tags: one for each person who went in, turned face down when they did not come out. Almost all of them are face down.

choices.text: Read the few tags that are face up

effects.log: Seven, in fifty years. The tea seller knows their stories: all seven went in at the new moon, all seven followed the stream, all seven came out with white hair.

choices.text: Hang your own tag on the wall

effects.log: The tea seller writes your name on a tag and hangs it, face up, very neatly. 'For now,' the tea seller says, kindly.

choices.text: Drink the tea and go home

effects.log: Very good tea. You go home. Some legends are better left as legends.

events.text: Inside the Valley of No Return the light is wrong: sunlight without a sun, shadows pointing the wrong way. The paths loop back on themselves. You have passed the same twisted pine three times. Something in the mist is following you, patient, on soft feet.

choices.text: Follow the stream, at the new moon, as the seven did

effects.log: Water does not lie. You follow it through the mist, and the loops untwist, and the soft feet fall behind.

choices.text: Turn and face what follows

ok.log: A grey shape in the mist, too many joints. It flinches from your blade and is gone. The paths straighten as if afraid of you.

fail.deathCause: the Valley of No Return
fail.log: It is everywhere at once. You run and fall and wake by the twisted pine, your hair gone grey at the temples.

choices.text: Mark every tree and walk out the way you came

effects.log: You tie a strip of cloth on every tree. It takes a day to undo three hours of walking. You come out at the valley mouth starving, alive.

events.text: The heart of the valley: a cave mouth in a cliff, an old stone door half open, a smell of incense older than any sect. On the threshold sits the skeleton of an explorer, cross-legged, as if meditating. In its lap is a jade slip.

choices.text: Go through the door

ok.log: Inside, an immortal's last meditation, written on the walls. You read for three days without eating. When you come out, your hair is white, and your eyes are very clear.

fail.deathCause: the immortal's cave in the Valley of No Return
fail.log: The words on the walls go into your mind like hooks. You come out raving, days later, and barely find the stream.

choices.text: Take the jade slip and leave the door alone

effects.log: The explorer got this far and sat down to read it. You read it on the way out: the explorer's name, a village, an apology. You will carry it home.

choices.text: Bow to the explorer and turn back

effects.log: Some doors are not for you. You bow, and leave, and the mist lets you go as if relieved.

events.text: Back at the valley mouth, the tea seller looks up and drops the teapot. Your tag is still face up on the wall.

choices.text: Turn another tag face up

effects.log: You give the tea seller the jade slip's name. The tea seller finds the tag, very old, and turns it over, and hangs it beside yours.

choices.text: Tell the tea seller what is inside

effects.log: The tea seller listens to it all, then writes it on a tag and hangs it by the door: THE STREAM, AT THE NEW MOON. People will still go in. More will come out.

choices.text: Drink the tea, and say nothing

effects.log: The tea seller pours, and does not ask. Your white hair says enough.

events.arc: The Mad Old Master of Cold Pine Ridge
events.text: On Cold Pine Ridge lives an old master who challenges every martial artist who passes and fights until one of them cannot stand. He has not lost in forty years. Nobody knows his name. The woodcutters call him Grandfather Snow and leave rice at the foot of the ridge.

choices.text: Ask the woodcutters about his fighting

effects.log: 'He always opens with the same move,' one says. 'A slow palm, like snow falling. Everybody blocks it. That is the mistake.'

choices.text: Leave rice at the foot of the ridge too

effects.log: You leave a bowl. In the morning it is gone, washed, and set back upside down on the stone.

choices.text: Take another road

effects.log: You go round. From the far ridge you see a tiny figure in white on Cold Pine Ridge, practising alone in the snow, beautifully.

events.arc: The Mad Old Master of Cold Pine Ridge
events.text: On the ridge, an old man in white steps out from the pines and bows. 'A guest. Good. Fight me.' His eyes are bright and far away, and very sad. He raises one hand in a slow palm, like snow falling.

choices.text: Fight him

ok.log: You do not block the slow palm; you step inside it. The fight that follows is the hardest of your life, and at the end the old master sits down in the snow, laughing, defeated for the first time in forty years.

fail.deathCause: the mad old master of Cold Pine Ridge
fail.log: You block the slow palm. Everybody does. You wake at the foot of the ridge, wrapped in a blanket, a bowl of rice beside you.

choices.text: Step inside the slow palm and refuse to strike

effects.log: You step inside it, as the woodcutter said, and then simply stand there, too close for him to fight, and wait. He stares at you. Then he lowers his hand.

choices.text: Bow, and say you came to bring rice

effects.log: The old man blinks. The far-away look clears for a moment. 'Rice?' He sits down on a rock. You give him the rice, and he eats it, and you sit with him.

choices.text: Decline and walk back down the ridge

effects.log: 'Coward,' he calls after you, cheerfully. 'Come back when you are brave.' You do not feel like a coward. You feel alive.

events.arc: The Mad Old Master of Cold Pine Ridge
events.text: Grandfather Snow remembers, now and then, who he was: the master of a sect that was destroyed in a single night forty years ago while he was away fighting a duel he had wanted very much to win.

choices.text: Listen to the whole story

effects.log: He tells it, in pieces, over a whole day. Every disciple's name. The duel he won. The hall he came home to. You understand, now, why he fights everyone who passes.

choices.text: Help him find the hall's ruins

effects.log: Three days' walk. A burned hall, grown over with pines. He stands in it for a long time, and then starts to sweep it, and you help.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you the slow palm

effects.log: He teaches it, sometimes clear-eyed, sometimes not. It is the finest technique you have ever learned, and the saddest.

events.arc: The Mad Old Master of Cold Pine Ridge
events.text: The woodcutters find you on the road: Grandfather Snow has died on the ridge, sitting in the snow, in the slow-palm stance. He left nothing but a pair of straw sandals and, scratched on a rock, your name.

choices.text: Bury him in the ruins of his hall

effects.log: Among his disciples. You read their names from memory, as he told them to you. The pines are very quiet.

choices.text: Practise the slow palm on the ridge, once, for him

effects.log: Slow, like snow falling. The woodcutters watch, bareheaded. One of them says he looked like that, once, when he was young.

choices.text: Keep leaving rice at the foot of the ridge

effects.log: Every winter, a bowl. The woodcutters think you are mad. In the morning it is always gone. Foxes, probably.

events.text: The Nine-Storey Pagoda of the Western Lake is famous: a cultivator who climbs it faces a heart demon on each floor, their own fears given shape. Those who reach the top break through. Many come down mad. The abbot at the gate warns you: 'The demons know you better than you know yourself.'

choices.text: Ask the abbot how to pass a heart demon

effects.log: 'Do not fight it. It is you. Recognise it, and walk past.' The abbot's eyes are kind. 'Easy to say.'

choices.text: Meditate a month before you climb

effects.log: A month on a mat facing the lake, going through every fear you have, one by one. It is the most frightening month of your life, and nothing happens at all.

choices.text: Decline the climb

effects.log: The pagoda will be there. You are not ready. Knowing that is itself a kind of passing.

events.text: The fifth floor of the pagoda. The lamps go out. In the dark, someone you failed is waiting, with your own face behind their face, and they ask you, very gently, why you did not come back for them.

choices.text: Fight the demon

ok.log: You strike it down and it gets up, and you strike it down, until your arms are lead and the demon is smaller, and then gone. The stair to the sixth floor is open.

fail.deathCause: a heart demon in the Nine-Storey Pagoda
fail.log: Every blow you strike lands on yourself. You wake at the bottom of the stairs, and your qi is a tangle, and for a month you cannot sleep without a lamp.

choices.text: Recognise it, answer it, and walk past

effects.log: 'I was afraid,' you say. 'I am sorry.' The demon looks at you with your own eyes, and steps aside. It does not vanish. You did not expect it to.

choices.text: Turn and walk back down the stairs

effects.log: Five floors is more than most climb. You walk down in the dark with the demon's question following you all the way to the gate, where the abbot gives you tea.

events.text: The ninth floor. A bare room with a window over the lake. No demon. Only a mirror. In the mirror, you, as you are: every kindness and cruelty, every coward's moment, every brave one, plain as daylight.

choices.text: Break through, here, now

ok.log: You look at yourself without flinching until the mirror is only glass. Something in you opens like a window. The lake below is the colour of the sky.

fail.deathCause: the mirror at the top of the Nine-Storey Pagoda
fail.log: You look away. Only for a moment. The mirror cracks, and so does something in you. You walk down nine floors very slowly.

choices.text: Sit in front of the mirror and simply look

effects.log: You sit there until dark, looking. You do not break through. You do not need to. You know yourself, now, a little.

choices.text: Turn the mirror to the wall and look at the lake

effects.log: The lake is enormous and does not care who you are. It is very restful.

events.text: At the pagoda gate the old abbot is waiting with tea, as for everyone who comes down. 'Well?' the abbot asks. 'What did they look like?'

choices.text: Tell the truth

effects.log: You tell it all: the fifth floor, the mirror. The abbot listens and nods, and pours more tea. 'Mine was my mother,' the abbot says. 'Still is, some nights.'

choices.text: Say: like me

effects.log: The abbot laughs, delighted. 'Then you were paying attention.'

choices.text: Say nothing, and drink the tea

effects.log: The abbot nods. Most people who come down from the ninth floor say nothing. That is how the abbot knows they were there.

events.text: In Cloud City the wells have been bubbling, the dogs howl at noon, and the rats are leaving the granaries in long lines toward the hills. An old geomancer in the market says the earth dragon is turning over in its sleep.

choices.text: Follow the rats out of the city

effects.log: You feel foolish walking behind rats. That night, from the hills, you watch the city lamps shake, and go out, all at once.

choices.text: Ask the geomancer when

effects.log: 'Tonight or tomorrow. Do not sleep under a heavy roof.' The geomancer is packing. Nobody else is.

choices.text: Stay; old cities have old walls

effects.log: You sleep at the inn. In the middle of the night the bed walks across the room by itself.

events.text: The earthquake comes at night: a roar from under the ground, and the city shrugs like a waking ox. Roofs fall. The temple bell rings by itself, wildly. In the street, a wall is leaning over a family who are trying to dig a grandmother out.

choices.text: Hold the leaning wall while they dig

ok.log: You set your shoulder to the wall and it stops. It weighs as much as the world. The grandmother comes out, coughing, and you step back, and the wall falls where you were.

fail.deathCause: the earthquake at Cloud City
fail.log: A second shock. The wall comes down on you. They dig you out at dawn, alive, with your legs broken.

choices.text: Dig with them from the side

effects.log: You dig from the side away from the leaning wall, with your hands, with a pot. The grandmother is out in an hour, angry and alive.

choices.text: Lead the street to the open square

effects.log: Everyone out of the narrow lanes and into the square, away from walls. The aftershocks bring down half the street. Nobody is under it.

events.text: Cloud City in the grey dawn: smoke, dust, crying. The magistrate's office has fallen. Nobody is in charge. The granary is standing, and a crowd is gathering at its door.

choices.text: Open the granary fairly, and keep order

effects.log: You stand on the granary steps and divide the rice by street. People argue, then queue. The city eats.

choices.text: Organise the searches

effects.log: Street by street, house by house, a line of diggers and a list of names. By the third day you have found everyone who can be found.

choices.text: Bring the people from the hills back down to help

effects.log: The ones who left with the rats come back down with carts and food. Cloud City is rebuilt by the people who listened to rats.

events.arc: The Whirlpool of the Eastern Sea
events.text: Sailors on the eastern coast whisper about the Sea Eye: a whirlpool off the Turtle Islands that opens without warning on the full moon and swallows ships whole. A captain who passed near it says he saw a light at the bottom, like a lantern in a well.

choices.text: Ask how ships escape it

effects.log: 'You do not fight the turn. You row with it, faster, until it throws you out of the rim.' The captain shudders. 'Nobody believes that, at the time.'

choices.text: Book passage on a ship that avoids the full moon

effects.log: Three days' wait. The ship goes past the Turtle Islands under a half moon, and the sea is flat and boring and wonderful.

choices.text: Take the first ship out

effects.log: The ship sails on the fourteenth night of the month. The sailors look at the moon a lot.

events.arc: The Whirlpool of the Eastern Sea
events.text: The full moon off the Turtle Islands. The sea goes quiet, then begins to turn. The ship tilts. Ahead the water drops away into a vast spinning funnel, and at its bottom, very far down, a light.

choices.text: Leap from the ship to the rim and haul it with a rope

ok.log: You run across the turning water on qi and a prayer, loop the line round a rock of the Turtle Islands, and the crew hauls the ship out of the turn hand over hand.

fail.deathCause: the Sea Eye off the Turtle Islands
fail.log: The rim is not water, it is wind. You are thrown into the funnel and spat out a li away, half drowned, clinging to a spar.

choices.text: Shout to row with the turn, faster

effects.log: The captain thinks you are mad. Then does it. The ship whirls round the funnel faster and faster and is flung out of the rim like a stone from a sling.

choices.text: Lash yourself to the mast and hold on

effects.log: The ship goes round the funnel three times, and the wind tears the sails off, and then the whirlpool closes as suddenly as it opened. The ship is a wreck. Everyone is alive.

events.arc: The Whirlpool of the Eastern Sea
events.text: A fisherman on the Turtle Islands says that every sixty years the Sea Eye closes for good for a while, and the light at its bottom can be reached by diving: a sunken palace, they say, older than the empire.

choices.text: Dive for the light at low tide

effects.log: You dive and dive and find, very deep, a sea-worn gate, carved with turtles, and a lantern of a stone that glows by itself. You leave it. You take a carved shell.

choices.text: Leave the sea to keep its own

effects.log: The fisherman nods. 'Good. The ones who go down for the palace do not need a whirlpool to drown.'

choices.text: Mark the Sea Eye on the coastal charts

effects.log: Every chart in the harbour gets your mark: a ring and a moon. Ships give it a wide berth at the full moon now.

events.text: In the far south the Burning Mountain has been smoking for a month. The villages on its slopes have dug terraces into its rich black earth for six hundred years. The headman says the mountain has smoked before and they will not leave their fields. The springs, an old woman says, have gone hot.

choices.text: Climb up to the crater to look

effects.log: The crater floor is cracked and glowing like a kiln. The air tastes of eggs and iron. From the rim you can see the whole of the slope's villages, and how close they are.

choices.text: Help the old woman persuade her family to leave

effects.log: Her family leaves, grumbling, with their pigs. The headman calls them cowards. Two other families follow them.

choices.text: Respect the headman's choice

effects.log: Six hundred years. Who are you to say? You go down the mountain and do not look back for a long time.

events.text: Night. The Burning Mountain explodes. Fire leaps into the sky, and the ground shakes, and from the crater a river of glowing rock begins to pour down the slope toward the terraces and the sleeping villages.

choices.text: Cut a channel to turn the fire aside

ok.log: With qi and a mattock and fifty villagers behind you, you cut a ditch across the slope. The burning river reaches it, hesitates, and turns into the gorge. The village is saved.

fail.deathCause: the burning mountain's fire river
fail.log: The fire comes faster than the digging. You are caught on the wrong side of the ditch and only a leap across the glowing rock saves you, and not all of you.

choices.text: Wake the villages and lead them downhill

effects.log: House to house in the red dark. The headman is the last to come, carrying an ancestor tablet. At dawn the terraces are black stone.

choices.text: Show them the path you saw from the rim

effects.log: From the rim you saw the high ridge the fire cannot reach. You lead them along it in the dark, above the burning, to safety.

events.text: The Burning Mountain is quiet. The terraces are buried. The headman sits on the black rock where the village was, with the ancestor tablet in his lap.

choices.text: Help them find new fields

effects.log: A valley two days north, empty and wet. The villagers plant it, complaining that the soil is not black. In ten years they have forgotten to complain.

choices.text: Sit with the headman

effects.log: He talks about six hundred years of terraces, and you listen. At the end he says: 'The old woman was right. I should have listened to her.' He says it to her, later.

choices.text: Climb back to the cooled crater

effects.log: The crater floor has cooled to black glass. In it, here and there, red crystals like frozen fire. You take one. It is warm in your hand for years.

events.text: Years later, seedlings are growing out of the black rock of the Burning Mountain's slope. The first new terrace has been dug, by the headman's grandchildren. They have built it above the high ridge.

choices.text: Help dig the second terrace

effects.log: Black rock and new earth, a terrace above the ridge. The grandchildren argue about where to put the shrine. You suggest the ridge.

choices.text: Teach them the signs: the springs, the smoke

effects.log: They listen. They will listen to their grandmother, too, next time.

choices.text: Leave a stone at the ridge with the date

effects.log: The year the mountain woke. The way the fire went. A stone is a long memory.

events.text: A secret realm has opened in the sky over the northern plains: a door of light, a world inside it, spirit herbs, old treasure. A hundred cultivators have gone in. The old ones say a secret realm that opens by itself also closes by itself, and does not wait for anyone.

choices.text: Go in, and watch the door

effects.log: Inside: a world of floating islands and strange birds. You never let the door out of your sight. Others wander off, laughing, into the islands.

choices.text: Ask how long it will stay open

effects.log: 'Nine days. Or three. Or until someone takes its heart.' The old cultivator shrugs. 'Nobody ever knows.'

choices.text: Stay outside and sell water to those who come out

effects.log: Very profitable. You watch them come out, laden and laughing, and wonder what you missed.

events.text: Inside the secret realm, a scream: someone has pulled a glowing crystal from an altar on the highest island, and the whole world shudders. The islands are falling. The sky is cracking. The door, far off, is flickering.

choices.text: Run for the door across the falling islands

ok.log: Island to island as they drop, the door shrinking ahead of you. You dive through as it snaps shut, and land rolling on the northern grass.

fail.deathCause: a collapsing secret realm
fail.log: An island falls under you into the dark. You climb back to the door with your arms torn, and fall through it half dead.

choices.text: You never lost sight of the door: walk out

effects.log: You are already beside it. You step out onto the grass, and stand there, holding the door edge with your qi for those running behind you.

choices.text: Hold the falling island steady for the others

effects.log: With every scrap of qi, you hold one island still while twenty people run across it. Then it falls, with you, and you are spat out of the realm onto the plain.

events.text: On the northern plain, where the secret realm was, there is a ring of scorched grass. Some came out. Some did not. The one who pulled the crystal is sitting in the middle of the ring, alone, holding it.

choices.text: Take the crystal from them and bury it

effects.log: It is warm and humming. You bury it deep in the plain. Perhaps one day the realm will grow again from it.

choices.text: Help them carry the guilt

effects.log: You sit with them. They pulled it without knowing. They will know forever. You tell them that the ones who got out, got out.

choices.text: Ask what was inside the crystal

effects.log: A whole world, they say, in a stone. They let you hold it. You feel the islands, the birds, very small, far away, still falling.

events.arc: The Jade Seal That Drinks Life
events.text: An auction house is selling a jade seal from an ancient emperor's tomb: green, flawless, carved with a coiled dragon. The last three owners died within a year of buying it, of nothing in particular. The auctioneer calls this 'provenance'.

choices.text: Examine it closely before the bidding

effects.log: When your hand is near it, you feel your qi tug toward it, like water to a drain. It is not a seal. It is a mouth.

choices.text: Bid on it

effects.log: You win it for a terrible price. It is very beautiful. That night you feel tired, very tired, for no reason.

choices.text: Warn the rich buyer who wins it

effects.log: The rich buyer laughs at you. A year later you hear of the funeral.

events.arc: The Jade Seal That Drinks Life
events.text: The jade seal is in your house, or a rich man's house that you have been asked to visit. The rich man is grey and wasted, and smiles at the seal on the desk like a lover. Your own qi is draining toward it across the room.

choices.text: Break the seal

ok.log: You strike it with everything you have. The jade cracks with a sound like a scream, and a cold wind blows out of it, and the grey goes out of the rich man's face. And yours.

fail.deathCause: the jade seal that drinks life
fail.log: The seal drinks your strike like water. You fall beside the desk, grey as the rich man, and wake a week later in a healer's house, years older.

choices.text: Wrap it in lead and drop it in the river

effects.log: Lead foil, a box, a bridge at midnight. The pull stops as soon as the box closes. The river is very deep there.

choices.text: Get the rich man out of the room

effects.log: You drag him out into the garden, protesting. In the sunlight he weeps and does not know why. You lock the door behind you.

events.arc: The Jade Seal That Drinks Life
events.text: A tomb inspector of the Board of Rites has heard about the seal and comes to ask where it came from. The emperor whose tomb it was, the inspector says, made a pact for a long life. The seal was the other half of the pact.

choices.text: Help the inspector seal the tomb properly

effects.log: A day in an ancient tomb with an inspector who knows exactly where to step. The inspector puts the broken seal back in the coffin.

choices.text: Ask how long the emperor lived

effects.log: Two hundred years. The inspector smiles thinly. 'And every one of his ministers died young.'

choices.text: Report the auction house to the Board

effects.log: The auction house is fined. Its next catalogue lists only very boring pots.

events.arc: The Frost Demon of the North
events.text: Beyond the northern wall, the frontier villages are freezing in midsummer: frost on the barley, ice in the wells, a white mist that walks against the wind. A garrison soldier says a frost demon has come down from the ice fields, and that where it breathes, people do not wake up.

choices.text: Ask how the frost demon is fought

effects.log: 'Fire does nothing. Swords do nothing. The old shamans say it hates warmth from inside, the warmth of a breath.' The soldier shrugs. 'Whatever that means.'

choices.text: Help the villages light fires

effects.log: Fires in every house, all night, every night. The frost stops at the doors. It waits.

choices.text: Go back south of the wall

effects.log: You go back. The garrison closes the gate behind you, and the wind from the north is very cold.

events.arc: The Frost Demon of the North
events.text: The white mist comes into the village at midnight, walking upright, against the wind. Everything it touches turns to frost: the fences, the dogs, the doorways. In its middle, a shape, tall and thin and white, breathing out.

choices.text: Fight it with your blade

ok.log: Your blade shatters on it. Your qi does not. You drive heat from your dantian through your hands into it until the white shape melts into mist and the mist into rain.

fail.deathCause: the frost demon of the north
fail.log: Its breath touches you. Your blood slows. You lie in the frost, and only the village fires bring you back.

choices.text: Breathe your own warm qi into the mist

effects.log: Warmth from inside. You breathe out, slow and hot, and the mist recoils from your breath like a hand from a stove. The shape hisses and draws back toward the ice fields.

choices.text: Keep the fires burning and the people inside

effects.log: All night the frost demon walks round the houses, breathing, and cannot get past the fires. At dawn it goes back to the north.

events.arc: The Frost Demon of the North
events.text: In the ice fields beyond the frontier, in a cave of blue ice, there is the frost demon's heart: a block of ice with something inside it, curled, like a sleeping child.

choices.text: Melt the ice and see what is inside

ok.log: Slowly, with your own breath, the ice melts. Inside is an ancient shaman, curled in meditation, who opens frost-white eyes and thanks you, and dies, at peace.

fail.deathCause: the frost demon's heart in the ice cave
fail.log: The cold comes out of the ice into you. You stagger out of the cave, and for a year you are never warm.

choices.text: Seal the cave with fire and stone

effects.log: You build a wall across the cave mouth and burn a fire against it for three days. The frost stops coming south.

choices.text: Leave it sleeping, and go

effects.log: You leave it. Some things should sleep. The frontier villages stay warm, mostly.

events.arc: The Frost Demon of the North
events.text: The frontier villages have their barley back. The garrison soldier, now an officer, tells you the old shamans have a new song, about the one who breathed on the frost.

choices.text: Ask to hear the song

effects.log: It is very long and very sad and you are much taller in it. The shamans sing it at the midsummer fire.

choices.text: Ask about the shaman in the ice

effects.log: A shaman who tried to stop a winter from coming, centuries ago, and became the winter. The song is really about that shaman.

choices.text: Stay a winter at the frontier

effects.log: A real winter, the ordinary kind. It is very cold and you are very happy to be cold in the ordinary way.

events.text: In the bamboo forests of the west, cultivators wake in the morning weak and empty, their qi drained as if by leeches. On their pillows, grey dust. A herbalist says it is the ash moths, which feed on qi at night, and come in clouds once every forty years.

choices.text: Ask what drives the moths off

effects.log: 'Mugwort smoke. They hate it. And a closed mind: they find you by your circulating qi, like moths to a lamp.'

choices.text: Buy mugwort and hang it by your bed

effects.log: The room smells like a temple. In the morning there is grey dust on the windowsill but not on your pillow.

choices.text: Meditate as usual and see

effects.log: In the morning, grey dust on your pillow and a hollow in your dantian like a missing tooth.

events.text: A cloud of ash moths comes out of the bamboo at dusk, millions of them, grey and soft and silent, pouring through the village like smoke. Where they settle on cultivators, the cultivators fall down, drained.

choices.text: Burn your qi bright and lure them away

ok.log: You circulate your qi as hard as you can, a lamp in the dark. The whole cloud follows you out of the village into the bamboo, where you stop your qi dead and drop, and they lose you.

fail.deathCause: a cloud of qi-eating ash moths
fail.log: They find you all at once. You fall in the bamboo, drained to the bone, and wake at noon empty as a husk.

choices.text: Light mugwort fires around the village

effects.log: A ring of bitter smoke. The cloud swirls against it and cannot come in. The cultivators inside are safe.

choices.text: Close your mind and tell everyone to do the same

effects.log: Stop circulating. Breathe like a farmer. The moths find nothing and drift on through the village and away.

choices.text: Hide in the well

effects.log: You climb down the bucket rope into the cold dark. Above you, the grey cloud passes. You come up at dawn shaking and full.

events.text: The ash moth cloud has passed west. Behind it, the village is full of drained cultivators, weak as children. The herbalist has a remedy, but it needs a thousand-year ginseng from the mountain.

choices.text: Climb the mountain for the ginseng

effects.log: Three days on the cliffs, a root as long as your forearm, shaped like a little old man. The herbalist makes a broth. The village recovers.

choices.text: Share your own qi with the weakest

effects.log: One by one, your hand on their backs, your qi into their dantian. It leaves you weak for a month. It leaves them alive.

choices.text: Write down the moths' habits for forty years from now

effects.log: Mugwort, closed minds, the well. Forty years from now, someone will need this.

events.arc: Your Name on the Depot's List
events.text: A eunuch you once saw at an inn sends you a gift: a fine fan, very elegant. Folded into it, a list in a tiny hand: twelve names marked for the Eastern Depot's attention this year. Your name is the ninth. There is no note.

choices.text: Find out who else is on the list

effects.log: Honest censors, a sect leader who refused a bribe, a poet. Good company. Bad sign.

choices.text: Thank the eunuch, carefully

effects.log: You send a gift back, very carefully worded. The eunuch's reply says only: 'Do not go to the capital this year.'

choices.text: Burn the fan

effects.log: You burn it. The list is in your head now. You cannot burn that.

events.arc: Your Name on the Depot's List
events.text: Agents of the Eastern Depot come for you at an inn in the hills: twenty, in brown, with silk cords and crossbows. They have a warrant. They do not intend to bring you to the capital alive.

choices.text: Fight your way out

ok.log: Twenty is a lot. You are a lot more. When it is over the inn is wrecked and the agents are running down the hill without their cords.

fail.deathCause: the Eastern Depot's agents
fail.log: The crossbows find you three times. You get out over the roof and down a gully, and lie in the river reeds for two days.

choices.text: Go out the back before they come in

effects.log: You were told not to go to the capital. You also learned not to sleep where you said you would. You are on a horse and gone when they kick the door.

choices.text: Surrender, and trust the law

effects.log: They bind you and take you down the hill. On the road, an honest censor's escort meets them, by chance or not. The warrant is not in order. You are released, with bruises.

events.arc: Your Name on the Depot's List
events.text: The eleven other names on the list are in danger too. Some do not know. A censor and a poet are in the capital itself.

choices.text: Go to the capital and warn them

ok.log: Twenty days of back roads and a night climb over the capital wall. You warn the censor and the poet. Both live through the year.

fail.deathCause: the Eastern Depot at the capital gate
fail.log: The Depot catches you at the capital gate. You escape, wounded, but the warnings do not reach everyone.

choices.text: Send coded letters by merchants

effects.log: Eleven letters, eleven merchants, eleven codes. Nine reach their names in time.

choices.text: Save yourself and go west

effects.log: You go west, far from the Depot's reach. You hear, over the year, which names on the list stopped being names.

events.arc: Your Name on the Depot's List
events.text: A new emperor. The Eastern Depot is purged; its chief is sent to sweep a tomb. In the purge, a list of all the Depot's targets is published. Your name is on it, with a note: 'Not found.'

choices.text: Frame the published list and hang it on your wall

effects.log: NOT FOUND, it says, under your name. Visitors laugh. You laugh more.

choices.text: Visit the eunuch who warned you

effects.log: The eunuch is old and retired, in a little house with a garden. You bring tea. Neither of you mentions the fan.

choices.text: Visit the censor and the poet

effects.log: The censor is the new chief censor. The poet has written a poem about a fan. It is very good, and very dangerous, and safe now.

events.arc: The Ghost Ship of the River Mouth
events.text: At the river mouth, fishermen will not go out on foggy nights: a ghost ship sails there, they say, with lanterns that burn green and a crew of the drowned who call out for help in the voices of people you know.

choices.text: Ask when it was last seen

effects.log: 'Every fog this month. Before that, never.' The fisherman frowns. 'Ghosts do not usually start so suddenly.'

choices.text: Watch from the harbour wall on a foggy night

effects.log: Green lanterns, far out in the fog, and voices calling. And something else: the creak of oars, many oars, very much alive.

choices.text: Stay in on foggy nights

effects.log: You stay in. The fishermen nod approvingly. Somebody's warehouse is emptied that night.

events.arc: The Ghost Ship of the River Mouth
events.text: Fog. You are out on the water in a borrowed boat, and the green lanterns come sliding out of the grey: a black hull, drowned faces painted on the sails, and voices calling your name. Close up, the voices are coming from men with speaking trumpets. Smugglers.

choices.text: Board the ghost ship

ok.log: Over the rail, into a crew of very frightened smugglers who had been counting on fear. The green lanterns go over the side. The cargo goes to the magistrate.

fail.deathCause: smugglers on the ghost ship at the river mouth
fail.log: The smugglers are frightened but many. You are thrown back into the sea and pulled out by the fishermen, half drowned.

choices.text: Row back and tell the fishermen it is only smugglers

effects.log: The fishermen laugh, then stop laughing, then get their boat-hooks. By the next fog thirty fishing boats are waiting in the river mouth for the ghosts.

choices.text: Keep still in the fog and let it pass

effects.log: The ghost ship passes close enough to touch. A smuggler leans over the rail and looks straight at you, and does not see you.

events.arc: The Ghost Ship of the River Mouth
events.text: The ghost ship is beached, its painted sails torn down. The fishermen are using the green lanterns as decorations. The smuggler captain, in a cage on the quay, asks to speak to you.

choices.text: Listen to the captain

effects.log: The captain names a merchant in the city who paid for the whole trick, ghosts and all. The merchant's warehouse turns out to be full of things the river mouth's fishermen had lost.

choices.text: Ask whose idea the ghosts were

effects.log: 'Mine,' the captain says, with some pride. 'I heard the stories when I was small.' You almost admire it. Almost.

choices.text: Leave the captain to the magistrate

effects.log: You walk away. The fishermen hang a green lantern on the harbour wall for luck. Fog nights are just fog nights again.

events.text: A young swordsman with a white tassel has been travelling the province, challenging masters of your rank, one each month. Eleven so far. The swordsman has won eleven, and left each master alive, and taken each one's sword as a trophy.

choices.text: Ask how the swordsman fights

effects.log: 'Fast. Always the first move, from the left. And then waits for you to make a mistake.' The old master who says it rubs a scarred wrist.

choices.text: Ask why the swordsman does it

effects.log: Nobody knows. Some say a vow. Some say pride. One says the swordsman cries after every duel, alone.

choices.text: Avoid the province this year

effects.log: You go elsewhere. The swordsman's tally reaches fifteen.

events.text: The swordsman with the white tassel finds you at a ferry landing, and bows. 'You are the twelfth.' The ferry passengers back away. The young face is very tired, and very polite.

choices.text: Accept the duel

ok.log: The first move comes from the left. You are already there. It is the longest, cleanest duel of your life, and at the end, for the first time, the swordsman loses.

fail.deathCause: a duel at the ferry landing
fail.log: The first move comes from the left and you are not there. You wake on the landing without your sword, and alive, as promised.

choices.text: Refuse the duel, politely

effects.log: The swordsman blinks. Nobody has refused before. 'Then you are not the twelfth.' The swordsman takes the next ferry, looking almost relieved.

choices.text: Ask the swordsman why

effects.log: The tired face looks at you for a long time. 'Because my master was killed by a master of your rank, and I do not know which one.' The duel is postponed. You talk all evening.

events.text: The swordsman with the white tassel has given back all eleven swords, it is said, one by one, with apologies, and is living in a hut on the ridge above the ferry landing.

choices.text: Climb up and visit

effects.log: Tea, silence, two swords leaning by the door. 'I did not know what to do with myself when I stopped,' the swordsman says. You teach the swordsman to fish.

choices.text: Help find the master's killer

effects.log: Old records, a name, a grave. The killer died years ago, alone. The swordsman sits at the grave all night, and comes down free.

choices.text: Ask for a friendly rematch

effects.log: No trophies this time. The swordsman laughs for the first time you have seen and draws. It is the best duel of your life.

events.text: The great horse fair on the northern plain: ten thousand horses in pens of rope and stakes. A horse dealer with one eye points at the sky in the west, which is a dirty yellow. 'Dust storm,' the dealer says. 'Horses hate it. If the pens go, get behind something solid.'

choices.text: Ask which pens are weakest

effects.log: 'The wild ones from the steppe. In the east corner. Rope and hope.' The dealer spits. 'Do not be east of them when the dust comes.'

choices.text: Help the dealer double the ropes

effects.log: An afternoon of ropes and stakes. The dealer's pens are the best on the plain. The dealer gives you a drink of mare's milk, which is a terrible mistake.

choices.text: Buy a horse and leave before the storm

effects.log: A sturdy bay mare, a good price. You leave the fair as the yellow sky comes on.

events.text: The dust storm hits the horse fair at noon. The steppe horses in the east corner scream and break their ropes, and then a thousand horses are running blind through the fair, through stalls and tents and people.

choices.text: Pull a fallen child out of the stampede

ok.log: You dive between hooves and come out with the child under your arm, behind an overturned cart, in a storm of dust and noise.

fail.deathCause: the stampede at the horse fair
fail.log: A horse catches you. You are trampled and thrown, and only the cart saves you from the rest.

choices.text: Get behind the dealer's double-roped pens

effects.log: The dealer's pens hold. You and fifty other people crouch behind them as the stampede goes round them like a river round a rock.

choices.text: Run west, away from the east corner

effects.log: You run west, into the wind. The stampede goes east, with the wind. You are blasted with sand and alive.

choices.text: Turn over a cart and shelter behind it

effects.log: You heave a cart on its side and drag three strangers behind it. The horses part around it.

events.text: After the storm the plain is strewn with broken tents and loose horses. The one-eyed dealer is rounding up horses with a lasso pole, and looks at you. 'Help? A horse for your trouble.'

choices.text: Help round up the horses

effects.log: Two days in the saddle chasing horses across the plain. The dealer gives you the best of the steppe horses, the one that started it all.

choices.text: Help find the people instead

effects.log: A day searching the wreckage. Most are found. You bring a lost grandmother to her family on the back of a borrowed horse.

choices.text: Sit down and drink mare's milk with the dealer

effects.log: It is still terrible. The dealer tells you about thirty horse fairs and nine stampedes. You laugh until your ribs hurt.

events.text: The sky to the south is a brown cloud that moves against the wind. An old farmer stands at the edge of his ripening millet with his hat in his hands. 'Locusts,' he says. 'When they go, the hungry come. Bandits are only hungry people with clubs.'

choices.text: Help beat drums in the fields to drive them off

effects.log: A whole village beating pots and drums. The locusts eat half the fields anyway. Half is better than none.

choices.text: Help harvest early, green

effects.log: Half-ripe millet, all hands, day and night. The locusts arrive to empty fields and move on.

choices.text: Leave the region

effects.log: You leave. Behind you the brown cloud settles on the valley.

events.text: Winter after the locust year. On the road through the starving valley, a dozen thin people with clubs and sickles step out in front of you. They are not bandits. They are farmers. One of them is the old man with the hat.

choices.text: Fight your way through

ok.log: You go through them without hurting anyone badly. They are too weak to stop you. Behind you, someone is crying.

fail.deathCause: starving farmers on the valley road
fail.log: Desperation makes them brave. A sickle cuts your arm before they scatter.

choices.text: Give them everything in your pack

effects.log: Rice, dried meat, silver. The old man takes it and cries. 'We are not bandits,' he says. 'We were not bandits.'

choices.text: Lead them to the town granary and argue for them

effects.log: The magistrate opens the granary, a little, when you stand in front of the gate with a dozen starving farmers behind you.

events.text: Spring. The old farmer's millet is coming up green. He sees you on the road and comes out with a bowl of thin millet porridge, which is everything he has, and holds it out.

choices.text: Eat it, and thank him

effects.log: It is the most precious bowl of porridge you have ever eaten. You eat every grain.

choices.text: Share it with him

effects.log: Half each, on the edge of the field. He tells you about his grandchildren. The millet looks good this year, he says.

choices.text: Ask how the village kept its seed

effects.log: 'We hid it from ourselves,' he says. 'In the shrine. Even when we were starving. Even the children knew.' You do not know what to say.

events.text: A night barge on the Grand Canal, packed with passengers and lamp oil in jars. The bargemaster is drunk and the cook is frying fish on an open brazier beside the oil. A sailor mutters that it happens every year somewhere on the canal.

choices.text: Move the brazier away from the oil jars

effects.log: The cook shouts at you. You move it anyway, to the stern. The sailor grins at you and helps.

choices.text: Find where the buckets and the rope are

effects.log: Two buckets, a coil of rope, a small boat on a tow line. You remember where they are, and feel foolish.

choices.text: Sleep at the bow, as far from the oil as you can

effects.log: You sleep at the bow with your boots on.

events.text: Midnight. A jar breaks, oil runs across the deck, and the barge goes up in a roar of flame. Sixty people are screaming. The canal is black and cold and the bank is far.

choices.text: Fight the fire with buckets

ok.log: Bucket after bucket, with the sailor. You keep the fire in the stern while the passengers go over the bow into the small boat and onto passing barges.

fail.deathCause: the fire on the Grand Canal
fail.log: The oil burns on the water. You are caught by the flames and go over the side, burned, into the cold.

choices.text: Cut the small boat loose and load it with children

effects.log: You know where the small boat is. You haul it alongside and hand the children down into it, one by one, while the deck burns.

choices.text: Jump and swim for the bank

effects.log: The canal is cold. You swim. On the bank you turn and watch the barge burn, and hear the passing boats picking people out of the water.

events.text: The canal authorities are looking into the barge fire. The bargemaster says the cook started it. The cook says the passengers did. The sailor looks at you.

choices.text: Tell them the truth: oil, a brazier, a drunk

effects.log: The bargemaster loses the licence. A new rule goes up at every canal lock: NO FIRE NEAR OIL.

choices.text: Speak for the cook, who tried to stop it

effects.log: The cook, sobbing, tried to throw the brazier overboard. Your word keeps the cook out of prison.

choices.text: Give a purse for the families of the lost

effects.log: Four were lost. You give a purse at the lock-house for their families.

events.arc: The Hanging Coffins of the Gorge
events.text: In a gorge in Sichuan, ancient coffins hang on wooden pegs high up the sheer cliff, put there by a people nobody remembers. A herb-gatherer tells you a rare cliff orchid grows beside the highest coffin. 'My brother climbed for it,' the gatherer says. 'The pegs are a thousand years old.'

choices.text: Ask what happened to the brother

effects.log: 'He is in the river.' The gatherer looks up at the cliff. 'He trusted the pegs.'

choices.text: Look at the pegs from below, for a long time

effects.log: Some pegs are black and hard as iron. Some are grey and split. The grey ones are the ones the brother trusted, you think.

choices.text: Leave the orchid to the coffins

effects.log: The coffins have waited a thousand years. The orchid can wait too.

events.arc: The Hanging Coffins of the Gorge
events.text: High on the cliff of the hanging coffins, the river a silver thread below. The orchid is three pegs away, beside the highest coffin. The next peg is grey and split.

choices.text: Trust the grey peg and swing across

ok.log: The peg cracks under your weight and holds just long enough. You swing to the black peg, and the orchid is in your hand.

fail.deathCause: a fall from the cliff of the hanging coffins
fail.log: The peg breaks. You fall, and catch a coffin's edge, and hang there with the ancient dead until you can climb down.

choices.text: Use only the black pegs, the long way round

effects.log: Black peg to black peg, the long way, past every coffin. It takes all day. The orchid is in your hand at sunset.

choices.text: Climb back down

effects.log: You climb down. The orchid nods in the wind beside the highest coffin, safe.

events.arc: The Hanging Coffins of the Gorge
events.text: The herb-gatherer whose brother fell is waiting at the foot of the cliff. In the river below, in the shallows, there is a jade bracelet caught on a rock. It was the brother's.

choices.text: Wade in and bring the bracelet out

effects.log: The gatherer holds it for a long time, sitting on the bank. 'He would have liked that it was someone careful,' the gatherer says.

choices.text: Give the gatherer the orchid

effects.log: The gatherer looks at it, and at the cliff, and weeps, and takes it to the temple to put on the brother's tablet.

choices.text: Bow to the coffins on the cliff

effects.log: A bow to the forgotten people up there, who were so careful with their dead. You leave the gorge quietly.

events.arc: The Siege of Plum Blossom Town
events.text: Rebel armies are moving in the west. In Plum Blossom Town, a walled market town, the garrison commander is old and the walls are older. A grain merchant tells you he has sold every sack he had to the town, at triple price, and is leaving tonight. 'When the merchants leave,' he says, 'so should you.'

choices.text: Stay, and help repair the walls

effects.log: A week of carrying stones to the weakest stretch, by the east gate. The old commander notices you. 'You have done this before?' 'No.' 'You are doing it well.'

choices.text: Ask the commander how many soldiers there are

effects.log: 'Two hundred. Half of them farmers with spears.' The commander laughs, without humour. 'The rebels have five thousand. But they are hungry and in a hurry.'

choices.text: Leave with the merchants

effects.log: You leave by the north road with the grain merchant's carts. Behind you, the next day, the smoke of the rebel camps rises in the west.

events.arc: The Siege of Plum Blossom Town
events.text: The rebels have surrounded Plum Blossom Town. For nine days they have shot arrows and shouted. Tonight their scouts are creeping toward the east gate, where the wall is weakest, with ladders.

choices.text: Lead a sortie out of the gate to burn the ladders

ok.log: Out of the postern in the dark with twenty farmers. The ladders burn. The scouts run. On the wall the old commander raises a torch and the whole town cheers.

fail.deathCause: the siege of Plum Blossom Town
fail.log: The scouts are waiting for exactly that. You fight your way back to the gate with half the farmers, and an arrow in your leg.

choices.text: Hold the stretch of wall you rebuilt

effects.log: The ladders go up against your stones and the stones hold. You push the ladders off one by one all night with a forked pole.

choices.text: Light every lantern on the east wall at once

effects.log: A hundred lanterns at once, and drums. The scouts think the wall is full of soldiers and creep back to their camp.

choices.text: Ring the alarm and wake the town

effects.log: Everybody on the wall with pots of boiling water and roof tiles. It is not pretty. It works.

events.arc: The Siege of Plum Blossom Town
events.text: The rebels have gone, hungry, in a hurry, west toward a richer town. Plum Blossom Town has its walls and its people. The old commander is sitting on the east gate steps with a cup of tea, looking very old.

choices.text: Sit with the commander

effects.log: 'Forty years in the army,' the commander says, 'and my best night was with farmers.' You drink tea on the steps until dawn.

choices.text: Ride west to warn the richer town

effects.log: Two days' hard riding. The richer town shuts its gates in time. The rebels break up outside it, starving, and go home.

choices.text: Help the farmers back to their fields

effects.log: The fields outside the walls are trampled. You help replant them, row by row, and the plum trees by the gate flower that spring as if nothing happened.
